title.zh: 卷二百九十 列傳第四十九 Cao Liyong, Sun JiYe, Zhang Qi, Yang Chongxun, Xia Shouen, Di Qing, Zhang Yu, Sun Jie, Guo Kui
title.raw: 卷二百九十 列傳第四十九 Cao Liyong, Sun JiYe, Zhang Qi, Yang Chongxun, Xia Shouen, Di Qing, Zhang Yu, Sun Jie, Guo Kui Volume 290 Biographies 49:

sentences.zh: 曹利用

translations.literal: Cao Liyong
translations.idiomatic: Cao Liyong

sentences.zh: 曹利用，字用之，趙州寧晉人。

translations.literal: Cao Liyong, styled Yongzhi, was a native of Ningjin in Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Liyong, courtesy name Yongzhi, came from Ningjin in Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父諫，擢明經第，仕至右補闕，以武略改崇儀使。

translations.literal: His father Jian passed the Mingjing examination, served as Right Supplementation Censor, and was transferred to Commissioner of Honored Ceremonies for his military talent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jian had passed the Mingjing examination and risen to Right Supplementation Censor before being reassigned as Commissioner of Honored Ceremonies on account of his military ability.

sentences.zh: 利用少喜談辯，慷慨有志操。

translations.literal: In youth Liyong delighted in debate and was generous and resolute in purpose.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Liyong loved argument and debate and carried himself with generous, steadfast purpose.

sentences.zh: 諫卒，補殿前承旨，改右班殿直，遷為鄜延路走馬承受公事。

translations.literal: When Jian died, Liyong was appointed Palace Front Attendant, then changed to Right Company Palace Guard, and was promoted to courier commissioner for official business on the Fuyan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After Jian's death he was appointed a Palace Front Attendant, then made a Right Company Palace Guard, and later promoted to courier commissioner on the Fuyan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，契丹寇河北，真宗幸澶州，射殺契丹大將撻覽，契丹欲收兵去，使王繼忠議和，擇可使契丹者。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde the Khitan raided Hebei; Emperor Zhenzong went to Chanyuan; the Khitan great general Talan was shot and killed; the Khitan wished to withdraw their troops; they sent Wang Jizhong to negotiate peace and sought someone who could be sent as envoy to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jingde era the Khitan invaded Hebei. Emperor Zhenzong went to Chanyuan, where a shot killed the Khitan general Talan. The Khitan then wished to pull back their army and sent Wang Jizhong to discuss peace, asking for someone who could serve as envoy to them.

sentences.zh: 利用適奏事行在，樞密院以利用應選，帝曰：「此重事也，毋輕用人。

translations.literal: Liyong happened to be reporting business at the imperial camp; the Bureau of Military Affairs nominated Liyong as fitting the selection; the Emperor said: "This is a weighty matter—do not employ a man lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Liyong happened to be presenting business at the traveling court, and the Bureau of Military Affairs put his name forward as a suitable choice. The emperor said, "This is a grave matter—do not appoint someone lightly."

sentences.zh: 」明日，樞密使王繼英又薦利用，遂授閤門祗候、崇儀副使，奉書詣契丹軍。

translations.literal: The next day Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Jiying again recommended Liyong; he was then appointed Gate Attendant and Vice Commissioner of Honored Ceremonies and sent with a letter to the Khitan army.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the commissioner of military affairs Wang Jiying recommended Liyong again, and he was appointed Gate Attendant and Vice Commissioner of Honored Ceremonies and sent with an imperial letter to the Khitan camp.

sentences.zh: 帝語利用曰：「契丹南來，不求地則邀賂爾。

translations.literal: The Emperor told Liyong: "The Khitan have come south; if they do not seek territory they will demand bribes."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Liyong, "The Khitan have marched south—if they are not after land, they will be pressing for gifts."

sentences.zh: 關南地歸中國已久，不可許；

translations.literal: The Guannan territory has belonged to China for a long time and cannot be granted;
translations.idiomatic: The Guannan territory has belonged to China for many years and must not be conceded;

sentences.zh: 漢以玉帛賜單于，有故事。

translations.literal: the Han bestowed jade and silks on the Chanyu—there is precedent for this.
translations.idiomatic: the Han used to bestow jade and silks on the Chanyu—there is precedent for that."

sentences.zh: 」利用憤契丹，色不平，對曰：「彼若妄有所求，臣不敢生還。

translations.literal: Liyong was angry at the Khitan; his countenance was unsettled; he replied: "If they presumptuously make some demand, your servant dares not return alive."
translations.idiomatic: Liyong burned with anger at the Khitan; his face showed it as he answered, "If they press some improper demand, your servant will not dare return alive."

sentences.zh: 」帝壯其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor was impressed by his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was heartened by his words.

sentences.zh: 利用馳至軍中，耶律隆緒母見利用車上，車軛設橫板，布食器，召與飲食，其從臣重行坐。

translations.literal: Liyong galloped to the army; the mother of Yelü Longxu saw on Liyong's carriage a crossboard set on the yoke and food vessels laid out; she summoned him to eat and drink, and his attendant ministers sat in double rows.
translations.idiomatic: Liyong rode swiftly to the Khitan camp. The mother of Yelü Longxu noticed on his carriage a crossboard fitted to the yoke and food vessels set out; she summoned him to eat and drink while his attendant ministers sat in two rows.

sentences.zh: 飲食畢，果議關南地，利用拒之。

translations.literal: When the meal was finished, they indeed discussed the Guannan territory; Liyong refused it.
translations.idiomatic: When the meal was over they did raise the question of Guannan, and Liyong refused.

sentences.zh: 遣其臣韓杞來報命，利用再使契丹。

translations.literal: They sent their minister Han Qi to report back; Liyong was again sent as envoy to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: They sent their minister Han Qi to carry their reply, and Liyong was dispatched to the Khitan a second time.

sentences.zh: 契丹母曰：「晉德我，畀我關南地，周世宗取之，今宜還我。

translations.literal: The Khitan mother said: "Jin owed us a debt of gratitude and gave us the Guannan territory; Emperor Shizong of Zhou took it; now it should be returned to us."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan empress dowager said, "Jin owed us gratitude and ceded Guannan to us; Emperor Shizong of Zhou seized it—now it ought to be returned to us."

sentences.zh: 」利用曰：「晉人以地畀契丹，周人取之，我朝不知也。

translations.literal: Liyong said: "The Jin gave the land to the Khitan; the Zhou took it—our dynasty knew nothing of this."
translations.idiomatic: Liyong replied, "The Jin ceded that land to the Khitan and the Zhou took it back—our dynasty had no part in either transaction."

sentences.zh: 若歲求金帛以佐軍，尚不知帝意可否，割地之請，利用不敢以聞。

translations.literal: If they ask yearly for gold and silks to support the army, I still do not know whether the Emperor's mind will approve; as for a request to cede territory, Liyong dares not report it.
translations.idiomatic: If you ask each year for gold and silks to support your armies, I still do not know whether the emperor would consent—but a request to cede territory is something I dare not even report."

sentences.zh: 」其政事舍人高正始遽前曰：「我引眾以來，圖復故地。

translations.literal: His Administrative Affairs Attendant Gao Zhengshi hastened forward and said: "I led the masses here intending to recover our former territory."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhengshi, an administrative affairs attendant, stepped forward abruptly and said, "I led our forces here to recover our former territory."

sentences.zh: 若止得金帛歸，則愧吾國人矣。

translations.literal: If we return having gained only gold and silks, we will have shamed our countrymen.
translations.idiomatic: If we go home with nothing but gold and silks, we will have shamed our people."

sentences.zh: 」利用曰：「子盍為契丹熟計，使契丹用子言，恐連兵結釁，不得而息，非國利也。

translations.literal: Liyong said: "Sir, why do you not think carefully on the Khitan's behalf? If the Khitan follow your words, I fear continuous warfare and festering enmity without cease—this is not to the state's advantage."
translations.idiomatic: Liyong said, "You would do well to think this through carefully for the Khitan. If they follow your counsel, I fear endless war and deepening enmity with no respite—that cannot serve your state's interest."

sentences.zh: 」契丹度不可屈，和議遂定，利用奉約書以歸。

translations.literal: The Khitan judged that he could not be bent; the peace agreement was then settled; Liyong returned bearing the treaty document.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that he could not be broken, the Khitan settled the peace, and Liyong returned bearing the treaty.

sentences.zh: 擢東上閤門使、忠州刺史，賜第京師。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and Prefect of Zhongzhou, and a residence in the capital was bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and made prefect of Zhongzhou, with a mansion granted him in the capital.

sentences.zh: 契丹遣使來聘，遂命利用迎勞之。

translations.literal: When the Khitan sent envoys on a friendly mission, he was ordered to welcome and entertain them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan sent envoys on a friendly visit, he was ordered to welcome and entertain them.

sentences.zh: 知宜州劉永規馭下殘酷，軍校乘眾怨，殺永規叛，陷柳城縣，圍象州，分兵掠廣州，嶺南騷動。

translations.literal: Liu Yonggui, prefect of Yizhou, governed his subordinates with cruelty; military officers, taking advantage of popular resentment, killed Yonggui and rebelled, seized Liucheng County, besieged Xiangzhou, and sent detachments to plunder Guangzhou; Lingnan was thrown into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yonggui, prefect of Yizhou, ruled his men with cruelty. Military officers, riding a wave of resentment, killed him and rebelled, took Liucheng County, besieged Xiangzhou, and sent detachments to raid Guangzhou, throwing all of Lingnan into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 帝謂輔臣曰：「向者司天占候當用兵，朕固憂遠方守將非其人，以起邊釁，今果然。

translations.literal: The Emperor told his chief ministers: "Earlier the Directorate of Astronomy's prognostications indicated warfare; I had indeed worried that frontier commanders far away were not the right men and would provoke border troubles—now it has come to pass."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his chief ministers, "The Directorate of Astronomy had lately foretold warfare. I had worried that distant frontier commanders might be the wrong men and provoke border trouble—and so it has proved."

sentences.zh: 曹利用曉方略，盡心於事，其以為廣南安撫使。

translations.literal: Cao Liyong understands strategy and devotes himself wholeheartedly to affairs; let him be made Pacification Commissioner of Guangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Liyong understands strategy and throws himself wholeheartedly into his duties—appoint him Pacification Commissioner of Guangnan."

sentences.zh: 」利用至嶺外，遇賊武仙縣。

translations.literal: Liyong reached beyond the ranges and encountered the rebels at Wuxian County.
translations.idiomatic: Liyong reached the far south and met the rebels at Wuxian County.

sentences.zh: 賊持健標，蒙采盾，衣甲堅利，鋒鏑不能入。

translations.literal: The rebels carried stout banners, covered themselves with colored shields, and wore armor so hard and sharp that blades and arrowheads could not penetrate.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels carried heavy standards, covered themselves with painted shields, and wore armor so tough that blades and arrowheads could not pierce it.

sentences.zh: 利用使士持巨斧長刀破盾，遂斬首以徇。

translations.literal: Liyong had his soldiers take great axes and long knives to break the shields, then beheaded the enemy and displayed the heads as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Liyong ordered his men to take up great axes and long knives to smash the shields, then beheaded the enemy and displayed the heads as a warning.

sentences.zh: 嶺南平，遷引進使。

translations.literal: When Lingnan was pacified, he was transferred to Commissioner of Introduction.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingnan was pacified he was promoted to Commissioner of Introduction.

sentences.zh: 歷客省使、嘉州防禦使，出為鄜延路總管。

translations.literal: He successively served as Guest Reception Commissioner and Defender of Jiazhou, then went out as overall commander of the Fuyan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Guest Reception Commissioner and Defender of Jiazhou, then was posted out as overall commander of the Fuyan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符七年，拜樞密副使，加宣徽北院使、同知院事，進知院事，遂拜樞密使、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu he was appointed Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, added as Northern Bureau Commissioner of the Palace Directorate and Associate Director of the Bureau, advanced to Director of the Bureau, and then appointed Commissioner of Military Affairs and Associate Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu he was made vice commissioner of military affairs, then added as northern bureau commissioner of the palace directorate and associate director, advanced to director, and finally appointed commissioner of military affairs and associate grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 利用在位既久，頗恃功。

translations.literal: Liyong had been in office a long time and came to rely somewhat on his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Having held office for many years, Liyong began to lean heavily on his past service.

sentences.zh: 天禧二年，輔臣丁謂、李迪爭論帝前，迪斥謂奸邪，因言利用與之為朋黨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianxi the chief ministers Ding Wei and Li Di argued before the Emperor; Di denounced Wei as treacherous and wicked and said that Liyong was in a faction with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianxi the chief ministers Ding Wei and Li Di quarreled before the emperor. Di denounced Wei as treacherous and declared that Liyong was his partisan ally.

sentences.zh: 利用曰：「以片文遇主，臣不如迪；

translations.literal: Liyong said: "In winning the ruler's favor through a brief memorial, your servant is not the equal of Di;
translations.idiomatic: Liyong said, "In winning the throne's favor through a brief memorial, I am no match for Di;

sentences.zh: 捐軀以入不測之虜，迪不逮臣也。

translations.literal: in risking my body to enter the unpredictable enemy, Di does not reach your servant's level."
translations.idiomatic: but in risking my life to enter the unpredictable enemy camp, Di does not reach my level."

sentences.zh: 」迪坐是免，而利用以檢校太師兼太子少保為會靈觀使，進尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Di was dismissed on this account, while Liyong was made Director of the Huiling Temple as Honorary Grand Preceptor and Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, and promoted to Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Di was dismissed on this account, while Liyong was made director of the Huiling Temple with the honorary titles of grand preceptor and junior tutor to the heir apparent, and promoted to right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 乾興初，加左僕射兼侍中、武寧軍節度使、景靈宮使，詔如曹彬給公使錢歲萬緡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianxing he was given additional titles as Left Vice Director, Palace Attendant, Military Commissioner of the Wuning Army, and Director of the Jingling Palace; an edict granted him, as with Cao Bin, ten thousand strings of public envoy funds yearly.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qianxing he was further made left vice director, palace attendant, military commissioner of the Wuning army, and director of the Jingling Palace, with an edict granting him ten thousand strings of public envoy funds each year, as had been done for Cao Bin.

sentences.zh: 契丹使者蕭從順桀驁，稱疾留館下，不時發。

translations.literal: The Khitan envoy Xiao Congshun was arrogant and overbearing; he claimed illness and remained at the hostel, not departing on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan envoy Xiao Congshun was arrogant and overbearing; he claimed illness and lingered at the guest house, refusing to depart on schedule.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣使問勞，相望於道。

translations.literal: The court repeatedly sent envoys to inquire after his health, one after another on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent envoys one after another to inquire after him, their processions filling the road.

sentences.zh: 利用請一切罷之，從順乃引去。

translations.literal: Liyong requested that all such visits be stopped; Congshun then withdrew and left.
translations.idiomatic: Liyong asked that all such attentions cease, and Congshun then took his leave.

sentences.zh: 加司空。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional title of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 舊制，樞密使雖檢校三司兼侍中、尚書令，猶班宰相下。

translations.literal: By old regulation, even if the commissioner of military affairs held honorary rank in the three directorates together with palace attendant or director of the Imperial Secretariat, he still ranked below the chief councillors.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulations, even when a commissioner of military affairs held honorary rank in the three directorates together with the titles of palace attendant or director of the Imperial Secretariat, he still ranked below the chief councillors.

sentences.zh: 乾興中，王曾由次相為會靈觀使，利用由樞密使領景靈宮使，時重宮觀使，詔利用班曾上，議者非之。

translations.literal: During Qianxing Wang Zeng went from secondary councillor to Director of the Huiling Temple; Liyong as commissioner of military affairs also headed the Jingling Palace; at that time the palace-temple directorship was highly valued; an edict placed Liyong's court rank above Zeng's, and critics disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianxing Wang Zeng moved from secondary councillor to director of the Huiling Temple while Liyong, as commissioner of military affairs, also headed the Jingling Palace. Because the palace-temple directorship was highly valued at the time, an edict placed Liyong's court rank above Zeng's, which drew criticism.

sentences.zh: 未幾，曾進昭文館大學士、玉清昭應宮使，將告謝，而利用猶欲班曾上，閤門不敢裁。

translations.literal: Before long Zeng was advanced to Academician of the Hall of Spreading Culture and Director of the Yujing Zhaoying Palace and was about to present thanks; yet Liyong still wished to rank above Zeng, and the Gate Office dared not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zeng was advanced to academician of the Hall of Spreading Culture and director of the Yujing Zhaoying Palace and was to present his thanks—but Liyong still wanted to rank above him, and the Gate Office dared not rule on the matter.

sentences.zh: 帝與太后坐承明殿久之，遣押班趣班，閤門惶懼莫知所出，曾抗聲目吏曰：「但奏宰臣王曾等告謝。

translations.literal: The Emperor and Empress Dowager sat in Chenming Hall for a long time and sent the usher to hurry the court formation; the Gate Office was fearful and did not know what to do; Zeng raised his voice and told the clerk: "Simply announce that the chief councillor Wang Zeng and others present their thanks."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and empress dowager sat in Chenming Hall for a long while and sent the usher to hurry the formation. The Gate Office was in a panic and did not know what to do. Zeng raised his voice and told the clerk, "Simply announce that the chief councillor Wang Zeng and others present their thanks."

sentences.zh: 」班既定，而利用怏怏不平。

translations.literal: Once the formation was settled, Liyong was resentful and displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Once the order was settled, Liyong was left resentful and displeased.

sentences.zh: 帝使同列慰曉之，仍詔宰臣、樞密使序班如故事，而利用益驕，尚居次相張知白上。

translations.literal: The Emperor had his colleagues console and instruct him, and also ordered that chief councillors and the commissioner of military affairs follow the old ranking—but Liyong grew still more arrogant and continued to place himself above the secondary councillor Zhang Zhibai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had his colleagues console and reason with him and also ordered that chief councillors and the commissioner of military affairs follow the old ranking—but Liyong grew still more arrogant and continued to place himself above the secondary councillor Zhang Zhibai.

sentences.zh: 尋召張旻於河陽，為樞密使，利用疑代己，始悔懼焉。

translations.literal: Soon Zhang Min was summoned from Heyang to be commissioner of military affairs; Liyong suspected he was to replace him and began to regret and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhang Min was summoned from Heyang to be commissioner of military affairs. Liyong suspected he was meant to replace him and began to feel regret and fear.

sentences.zh: 初，章獻太后臨朝，中人與貴戚稍能軒輊為禍福，而利用以勳舊自居，不恤也。

translations.literal: At first, when Empress Dowager Zhangxian held court, eunuchs and noble kin could somewhat raise or lower fortunes at will, but Liyong, placing himself among meritorious elders of the dynasty, paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Zhangxian first held court, eunuchs and noble kin could sway fortunes at will, but Liyong, counting himself among the dynasty's meritorious elders, paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 凡內降恩，力持不予，左右多怨，太后亦嚴憚利用，稱曰侍中而不名。

translations.literal: Whenever internal edicts granted favors, he firmly held back and would not grant them; those around the throne bore much resentment; the Empress Dowager also stood in awe of Liyong and addressed him as Palace Attendant without using his name.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever internal edicts granted favors, he firmly refused to carry them out, earning much resentment from those around the throne. The empress dowager herself stood in awe of him and addressed him as "Palace Attendant" without using his name.

sentences.zh: 利用奏事簾前，或以指爪擊帶鞓，左右指以示太后曰：「利用在先帝時，何敢爾邪？

translations.literal: When Liyong reported business before the curtain, he would sometimes strike his belt plaque with a fingernail; those beside him pointed this out to the Empress Dowager and said: "In the late emperor's time, how would Liyong have dared act thus?"
translations.idiomatic: When Liyong reported business before the curtain, he would sometimes tap his belt plaque with a fingernail. Those beside him pointed this out to the empress dowager and said, "In the late emperor's time, how would Liyong have dared behave like this?"

sentences.zh: 」太后頷之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager nodded.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager nodded.

sentences.zh: 利用奏抑內降恩難屢卻，亦有不得已從之者。

translations.literal: Liyong reported that it was hard to refuse internal edict favors repeatedly, and that there were times when he had no choice but to comply.
translations.idiomatic: Liyong reported that it was difficult to refuse internal edict favors repeatedly and that there were times when he had no choice but to comply.

sentences.zh: 人揣知之，或紿太后曰：「蒙恩得內降輒不從，今利用家媼陰諾臣請，其必可得矣。

translations.literal: People guessed this and some deceived the Empress Dowager, saying: "When I received grace and got an internal edict, Liyong would not comply; now an old nurse in Liyong's household secretly promised my request—surely it can be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: People sensed this, and some deceived the empress dowager, saying, "Whenever I received an internal edict Liyong would not comply—but now an old nurse in Liyong's household has secretly promised my request, so it will surely go through."

sentences.zh: 」下之而驗，太后始疑其私，頗銜怒。

translations.literal: The edict was issued and proved true; the Empress Dowager then first suspected his private dealings and bore considerable anger.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was issued and proved true. The empress dowager then first suspected his private dealings and nursed considerable anger.

sentences.zh: 內侍羅崇勳得罪，太后使利用召崇勳戒敕之，利用去崇勳冠幘，詬斥良久，崇勳恨之。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Luo Chongxun had committed an offense; the Empress Dowager had Liyong summon Chongxun to admonish him; Liyong removed Chongxun's cap and headcloth and reviled him at length; Chongxun bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendant Luo Chongxun had committed an offense. The empress dowager had Liyong summon him to deliver a reprimand. Liyong removed Chongxun's cap and headcloth and berated him at length, and Chongxun came to hate him.

sentences.zh: 會從子汭為趙州兵馬監押，而州民趙德崇詣闕告汭不法事。

translations.literal: It happened that his nephew Yan was military supervisor of Zhao Prefecture, and a man of the prefecture, Zhao Dechong, went to court to report Yan's unlawful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that his nephew Yan was military supervisor at Zhao Prefecture, and a local man named Zhao Dechong went to court to report Yan's misconduct.

sentences.zh: 奏上，崇勳請往按治，遂窮探其獄。

translations.literal: When the memorial reached the throne, Chongxun requested to go investigate and thoroughly probed the case.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, Chongxun asked to go investigate and thoroughly probed the case.

sentences.zh: 汭坐被酒衣黃衣，令人呼萬歲，杖死。

translations.literal: Yan was found guilty of being drunk and wearing yellow robes and having someone call out "Long live the Emperor"; he was beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was found guilty of being drunk, wearing yellow robes, and having someone shout "Long live the emperor!" He was beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 初，汭事起，即罷利用樞密使，加兼侍中判鄧州。

translations.literal: When the case against Yan first arose, Liyong was immediately removed as commissioner of military affairs and given the additional title of palace attendant with jurisdiction over Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the case against Yan arose, Liyong was removed as commissioner of military affairs and given the additional title of palace attendant with jurisdiction over Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 及汭誅，謫左千牛衛將軍、知隨州。

translations.literal: When Yan was executed, Liyong was demoted to General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard and made prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was executed, Liyong was demoted to general of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard and made prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 又坐私貸景靈宮錢，貶崇信軍節度副使，房州安置，命內侍楊懷敏護送；

translations.literal: He was again punished for privately lending out Jingling Palace funds, demoted to vice military commissioner of the Chongxin Army, and placed under restraint in Fangzhou, with the inner attendant Yang Huaimin ordered to escort him;
translations.idiomatic: He was punished again for privately lending out Jingling Palace funds, demoted to vice military commissioner of the Chongxin army, and placed under restraint in Fangzhou, with the inner attendant Yang Huaimin ordered to escort him;

sentences.zh: 諸子各奪二官，沒所賜第，籍其貲，黜親屬十餘人。

translations.literal: each of his sons was stripped of two ranks; the residence that had been granted was confiscated; his property was registered and seized; more than ten kinsmen were dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: each of his sons was stripped of two ranks, the mansion that had been granted him was confiscated, his property was registered and seized, and more than ten kinsmen were dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 宦者多惡利用，行至襄陽驛，懷敏不肯前，以語逼之，利用素剛，遂投繯而絕，以暴卒聞。

translations.literal: Many eunuchs hated Liyong; when they reached Xiangyang Post Station, Huaimin would not go forward and pressed him with words; Liyong had always been stubborn; he then hanged himself and died; it was reported as sudden death.
translations.idiomatic: Many eunuchs hated Liyong. When they reached Xiangyang post station, Huaimin would not go forward and pressed him with words. Liyong had always been unyielding; he hanged himself, and his death was reported as sudden.

sentences.zh: 後其家請居鄧州，帝惻然許之，命其子內殿崇班淵監本州稅。

translations.literal: Later his family requested to reside in Dengzhou; the Emperor compassionately granted it and ordered his son Yuan, an Inner Palace Attendant of the Honored Company, to supervise the prefecture's tax collection.
translations.idiomatic: Later his family asked permission to live in Dengzhou. The emperor compassionately agreed and ordered his son Yuan, an inner palace attendant of the Honored Company, to supervise tax collection in that prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明道二年，追復節度兼侍中，後贈太傅，還諸子官，賜諡襄悼，命學士趙概作神道碑，帝為篆其額曰「旌功之碑」，詔歸所沒舊產。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingdao his military commission and palace attendant title were posthumously restored; later he was given the posthumous title Grand Tutor; his sons' offices were returned; he was granted the temple name Xiangdao; Academician Zhao Gai was ordered to compose his spirit-way stele; the Emperor personally seal-scripted its title as "Stele Commemorating Merit"; an edict returned the confiscated former property.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingdao his military commission and palace attendant title were posthumously restored. Later he was given the posthumous title Grand Tutor, his sons' offices were returned, and he was granted the temple name Xiangdao. Academician Zhao Gai was ordered to compose his spirit-way stele, and the emperor personally wrote its title in seal script: "Stele Commemorating Merit." An edict returned the confiscated property.

sentences.zh: 利用性悍梗少通，力裁僥幸，而其親舊或有因緣以進者，故及於禍。

translations.literal: Liyong's nature was fierce and obstinate with little flexibility; he strove to cut off opportunists, yet some among his kin and friends advanced through connections—therefore he met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Liyong was by nature fierce and inflexible, and he worked hard to cut off opportunists—yet some among his kin and friends had advanced through connections, and that was how he came to ruin.

sentences.zh: 然在朝廷忠藎有守，始終不為屈，死非其罪，天下冤之。

translations.literal: Yet in court he was loyal and steadfast and would not yield to the end; his death was not for his true crimes; all under Heaven regarded it as unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in court he had been loyal and steadfast and never yielded. His death was not deserved, and people everywhere regarded it as an injustice.

sentences.zh: 孫繼鄴

translations.literal: Sun Jiye
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jiye

translations.literal: 〈Appended〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Appended biography〉

sentences.zh: 孫繼鄴，字元嗣，其先金陵人。

translations.literal: Sun Jiye, styled Yuansi, was originally from Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jiye, courtesy name Yuansi, came from Jinling.

sentences.zh: 祖謙，事李昪為長劍都指揮使，南伐閩，援兵不至，戰死。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qian served Li Bian as commander of the Long Sword Guard; in the southern campaign against Min, reinforcements did not arrive and he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qian had served Li Bian as commander of the Long Sword Guard. On the southern campaign against Min, reinforcements never arrived and he died in battle.

sentences.zh: 父承睿時為小校，憤將兵者不如期，致其父沒，乃刺殺之，亡去，轉徙淮、楚間。

translations.literal: His father Chengrui was then a junior officer; angered that the commander had not arrived on schedule and caused his father's death, he stabbed and killed him, fled, and wandered between the Huai and Chu regions.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengrui was then a junior officer. Angered that the commanding officer had not arrived on schedule and so caused his father's death, he stabbed the man and fled, wandering between the Huai and Chu regions.

sentences.zh: 久之，入京師，以策上太宗，授左班殿直，終左藏庫使。

translations.literal: After a long time he entered the capital, presented a stratagem to Emperor Taizong, and was appointed Left Company Palace Guard; he ended as Commissioner of the Left Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he entered the capital, presented a stratagem to Emperor Taizong, and was appointed a Left Company Palace Guard. He ended his career as commissioner of the Left Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 繼鄴初以三班奉職監涔陽酒稅。

translations.literal: Jiye at first served as a Third Company Attendant supervising the wine tax at Cenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiye began as a Third Company Attendant supervising the wine tax at Cenyang.

sentences.zh: 會宜州陳進反，曹利用辟以自隨，為前驅，破賊於象州大烏嶺。

translations.literal: When Chen Jin of Yizhou rebelled, Cao Liyong recruited him to accompany him; as vanguard he defeated the rebels at Dawu Ridge in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Jin of Yizhou rebelled, Cao Liyong recruited him to accompany him. Serving as vanguard, he defeated the rebels at Dawu Ridge in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以功遷左侍禁、端州兵馬監押。

translations.literal: For his merit he was transferred to Left Palace Guard and military supervisor of Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to Left Palace Guard and made military supervisor of Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 徙秦州永寧砦，總徒城洛門，改西頭供奉官。

translations.literal: He was moved to Yongning Stockade in Qinzhou, oversaw conscript labor to build Luomen city, and was changed to Western Head Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to Yongning Stockade in Qinzhou, oversaw conscript labor to build the city of Luomen, and was made a Western Head Attendant.

sentences.zh: 晁迥薦為閤門祗候，上御戎策十數事。

translations.literal: Chao Jiong recommended him as Gate Attendant; he presented more than ten items of military policy to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Jiong recommended him as Gate Attendant, and he presented more than ten items of military policy to the throne.

sentences.zh: 又用曹瑋薦，為鄜延路兵馬都監，徙知環州，累遷崇儀副使。

translations.literal: Again through Cao Wei's recommendation he became overall military supervisor of the Fuyan Circuit, was moved to serve as prefect of Huanzhou, and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Commissioner of Honored Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: On Cao Wei's recommendation he became overall military supervisor of the Fuyan Circuit, was transferred to serve as prefect of Huanzhou, and rose in stages to Vice Commissioner of Honored Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 會修築洪德砦，與總兵者論事不協，絀為冀州兵馬都監，起知保安軍，徙涇州。

translations.literal: When Hongde Stockade was being built, he disagreed with the overall commander on affairs and was demoted to military supervisor of Jizhou; he was then raised to command the Bao'an Army and transferred to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During construction of Hongde Stockade he fell out with the overall commander over policy and was demoted to military supervisor of Jizhou. He was then raised to command the Bao'an Army and transferred to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 使契丹。

translations.literal: He was sent as envoy to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as envoy to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 樞密使曹利用欲用之，繼鄴惡其權盛，陰知利用將有禍，數以疾辭，遂除左龍武軍統軍致仕。

translations.literal: Commissioner of Military Affairs Cao Liyong wished to employ him; Jiye disliked his swollen power, secretly knew that Liyong would meet with disaster, repeatedly declined on grounds of illness, and was then made retired as overall commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner of military affairs Cao Liyong wished to employ him, but Jiye disliked his swollen power, secretly foresaw that Liyong would come to ruin, and repeatedly declined on grounds of illness until he was granted retirement as overall commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 利用貶，復為崇儀副使，遷供備庫使、知石州，徙保州，領恩州刺史、知雄州。

translations.literal: When Liyong was demoted, Jiye was restored as Vice Commissioner of Honored Ceremonies, transferred to Commissioner of the Equipment Storehouse and prefect of Shizhou, moved to Baozhou, and held the titles of Prefect of Enzhou and prefect of Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Liyong was demoted, Jiye was restored as Vice Commissioner of Honored Ceremonies, made commissioner of the Equipment Storehouse and prefect of Shizhou, transferred to Baozhou, and given the titles of prefect of Enzhou and prefect of Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 累遷西上閤門使，擢為龍神衛四廂都指揮使、端州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and advanced to overall commander of the four companies of the Dragon Spirit Guard and Defender of Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and was advanced to overall commander of the four companies of the Dragon Spirit Guard and Defender of Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 出為環慶路副都總管，道改涇原路，兼知渭州。

translations.literal: He went out as deputy overall commander of the Huanqing Circuit, was en route transferred to the Jingyuan Circuit, and concurrently served as prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted out as deputy overall commander of the Huanqing Circuit, was transferred en route to the Jingyuan Circuit, and concurrently served as prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 建言：「蕭關故道，前控大川，善水草，賊騎所從出也。

translations.literal: He submitted a proposal: "The old road through Xiaoguan fronts a great river valley, has good water and pasture, and is the route by which enemy cavalry come forth."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a proposal: "The old road through Xiaoguan commands a great river valley with good water and pasture—it is the route enemy cavalry use to come forth."

sentences.zh: 誠得屬羌，與奉賜，且羈其酋領，使為藩籬，則可無西顧憂矣。

translations.literal: If we could truly win the subordinate Qiang, grant them stipends, and moreover restrain their chieftains so they serve as a barrier, then we could be free of worry over the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: If we could truly win over the subordinate Qiang with stipends and keep their chieftains in check so they serve as a barrier, we could be free of worry over the western frontier."

sentences.zh: 」為步軍都虞候，徙真定路，卒。

translations.literal: He was made Chief Adjutant of the Foot Soldiers, transferred to the Zhending Circuit, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief adjutant of the foot soldiers, transferred to the Zhending Circuit, and died.

sentences.zh: 張耆，字元弼，開封人。

translations.literal: Zhang Qi, styled Yuanbi, was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qi, courtesy name Yuanbi, came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 年十一，給事真宗藩邸，及即位，授西頭供奉官。

translations.literal: At age eleven he served in Prince Zhenzong's household; when Zhenzong ascended the throne, he was appointed Western Head Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he entered service in Prince Zhenzong's household. When Zhenzong ascended the throne, he was appointed a Western Head Attendant.

sentences.zh: 嘗與石知顒侍射苑中，連發中的，擢供備庫副使、帶御器械。

translations.literal: Once he attended archery in the garden with Shi Zhiyong and hit the target repeatedly in succession; he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Equipment Storehouse and Bearer of Imperial Arms.
translations.idiomatic: Once he attended an archery session in the garden with Shi Zhiyong and hit the target repeatedly in succession. He was promoted to vice commissioner of the Equipment Storehouse and bearer of imperial arms.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，契丹犯邊，以功遷南作坊使、昭州刺史、天雄軍兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: During Xianping the Khitan raided the frontier; for his merit he was transferred to Commissioner of the Southern Workshops, Prefect of Zhaozhou, and military controller of the Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping era the Khitan raided the frontier. For his service he was promoted to commissioner of the Southern Workshops, prefect of Zhaozhou, and military controller of the Tianxiong army.

sentences.zh: 邊兵未解，徙鎮州行營鈐轄，又徙定州。

translations.literal: Before the frontier troops were stood down, he was moved to military controller of the mobile camp at Zhenzhou, then again to Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before the frontier forces were stood down, he was transferred to military controller of the mobile camp at Zhenzhou, then again to Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹圍望都，耆與諸將從間道往援，比至，城已陷矣。

translations.literal: The Khitan besieged Wangdu; Qi and the generals took a bypath to relieve it; by the time they arrived, the city had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan besieged Wangdu. Qi and the other generals took a bypath to relieve the city, but by the time they arrived it had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 耆與敵戰，身被數創，殺契丹梟將。

translations.literal: Qi fought the enemy, received several wounds on his body, and killed a Khitan commander of renown.
translations.idiomatic: Qi fought the enemy, took several wounds, and killed a renowned Khitan commander.

sentences.zh: 遲明復戰，而王繼忠為契丹所執。

translations.literal: At dawn he fought again, while Wang Jizhong was captured by the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he fought again, while Wang Jizhong was captured by the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 耆還，因言天道方利先舉者，請大舉討之，及上興師出境之日。

translations.literal: Qi returned and then said that Heaven's way currently favored whoever moved first; he requested a major campaign to attack them, timed for the day when the sovereign raised troops and crossed the border.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi returned, he said that Heaven's way currently favored whoever struck first. He asked for a major campaign against the Khitan, timed to coincide with the day the emperor raised troops and crossed the border.

sentences.zh: 帝以問輔臣，以為不可。

translations.literal: The Emperor questioned the chief ministers about it; they considered it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted his chief ministers, who judged the proposal inadvisable.

sentences.zh: 遷昭州團練使、幷代州鈐轄。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regimental Commissioner of Zhaozhou and military controller of Bingzhou and Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to regimental commissioner of Zhaozhou and military controller of Bing and Dai prefectures.

sentences.zh: 明年，契丹兵復入，旁欲親征，耆奏邊事十餘條，多論兵貴持重及所以取勝者。

translations.literal: The next year Khitan troops invaded again; the Emperor wished to campaign in person; Qi submitted more than ten items on frontier affairs, mostly discussing that in warfare weightiness is prized and how victory may be won.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Khitan invaded again. The emperor wished to take the field in person, and Qi submitted more than ten memorials on frontier affairs, most of them arguing that armies should be handled with restraint and explaining how to win.

sentences.zh: 召還，入對，帝曰：「卿嘗請北伐，契丹入塞，與卿所請興師之日同，悔不用卿策。

translations.literal: He was summoned back and granted audience; the Emperor said: "You once requested a northern campaign; the Khitan entered the frontier on the same day you asked to raise troops—I regret not using your plan.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled for audience. The emperor said, "You once asked for a northern campaign. The Khitan entered the frontier on the very day you urged us to mobilize—I regret that we did not follow your plan.

sentences.zh: 今領守澶州而未得人，如何？

translations.literal: Now I am leading the defense of Chanyuan but lack the right man—what shall we do?"
translations.idiomatic: I am now directing the defense of Chanyuan but still lack the right man. What shall we do?"

sentences.zh: 」耆請行。

translations.literal: Qi requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: Qi volunteered to go.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，命為駕前西面鈐轄，令至澶州候契丹遠近。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and appointed him Western Military Controller before the Imperial Carriage, ordering him to go to Chanyuan and observe how near or far the Khitan were.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and made him western military controller before the imperial carriage, ordering him to Chanyuan to watch the Khitan's movements.

sentences.zh: 耆馳騎往，改東面排陣鈐轄。

translations.literal: Qi rode there at full speed and was changed to Eastern Array Formation Military Controller.
translations.idiomatic: Qi rode there at full speed and was reassigned as eastern array-formation military controller.

sentences.zh: 事平，會曹州趙諫告耆受金，為人求薦禮部，貶供備庫使、潞州都監。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, it happened that Zhao Jian of Caozhou reported that Qi had accepted gold to seek Ministry of Rites recommendations for others; he was demoted to Commissioner of the Equipment Storehouse and Chief Supervisor of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was restored, Zhao Jian of Caozhou reported that Qi had taken bribes to secure Ministry of Rites recommendations for others. Qi was demoted to commissioner of the Equipment Storehouse and chief supervisor of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，事稍辨，復官管勾皇城司。

translations.literal: After a long time the matter was somewhat clarified, and he was restored to office as overseer of the Imperial City Office.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while the matter was largely cleared up, and he was restored to office as overseer of the Imperial City Office.

sentences.zh: 帝以耆歷河東，稔邊事，召耆至宣和閣，問地里險易狀。

translations.literal: Because Qi had served in Hedong and was thoroughly familiar with frontier affairs, the Emperor summoned him to the Xuanhe Pavilion and asked about the terrain's difficulties and advantages.
translations.idiomatic: Because Qi had served in Hedong and knew frontier affairs well, the emperor summoned him to the Xuanhe Pavilion and questioned him about the terrain.

sentences.zh: 耆因言：「雲、應、蔚、朔四郡，間遣人以文移至幷、代間，非覘邊虛實，即欲熟道路。

translations.literal: Qi then said: "The four prefectures of Yun, Ying, Wei, and Shuo intermittently send people with official documents to the area between Bing and Dai—either to observe the frontier's strengths and weaknesses, or to become familiar with the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Qi then said, "The four prefectures of Yun, Ying, Wei, and Shuo keep sending men with official documents into the country between Bing and Dai—either to spy out our frontier's strengths and weaknesses or to learn the roads by heart.

sentences.zh: 宜密諭代州，使自雲、應、蔚至者由大石谷入，自朔至者由土墱入，餘間道皆塞之以示險。

translations.literal: It would be best secretly to instruct Daizhou that those coming from Yun, Ying, and Wei should enter by Dashigu, those from Shuo by Tuyong, and all other bypaths should be blocked to show the difficulty of the terrain."
translations.idiomatic: We should secretly instruct Daizhou that arrivals from Yun, Ying, and Wei must enter by Dashigu, those from Shuo by Tuyong, and that all other bypaths should be blocked to show how difficult the country is."

sentences.zh: 」景德罷兵，耆與曹璨、李神祐、岑保正閱軍籍，請汰罷癃者。

translations.literal: When the Jingde truce ended hostilities, Qi joined Cao Shen, Li Shenyou, and Cen Baozheng in reviewing military registers and requested the dismissal of the infirm.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jingde truce ended the war, Qi joined Cao Shen, Li Shenyou, and Cen Baozheng in reviewing military registers and asked that the infirm be weeded out.

sentences.zh: 遷英州防禦使、侍衛親軍馬軍都虞候。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Defender of Yingzhou and Chief Adjutant of the Horse Soldiers of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to defender of Yingzhou and chief adjutant of the horse soldiers of the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 從帝東封，遷絳州防禦使、殿前都虞候。

translations.literal: He accompanied the Emperor on the eastern Feng sacrifice and was transferred to Defender of Jiangzhou and Chief Adjutant of the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on the eastern Feng sacrifice and was transferred to defender of Jiangzhou and chief adjutant of the palace front.

sentences.zh: 時建玉清宮，耆奏疏謂殫國財力，非所以承天意。

translations.literal: At that time the Jade Purity Palace was being built; Qi submitted a memorial saying it would exhaust the state's finances and was not the way to fulfill Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: While the Jade Purity Palace was being built, Qi submitted a memorial arguing that the project would drain the state's finances and was no way to fulfill Heaven's intent.

sentences.zh: 遷相州觀察使、馬軍副都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Observation Commissioner of Xiangzhou and Vice Commander-in-Chief of the Horse Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to observation commissioner of Xiangzhou and vice commander-in-chief of the horse soldiers.

sentences.zh: 從祀汾陰，授威塞軍節度使，進宣徽南院使兼樞密副使。

translations.literal: He accompanied the sacrifice at Fenyin, was appointed Military Commissioner of the Weisai Army, and was advanced to Commissioner of the Southern Court of the Palace Secretariat together with Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the sacrifice at Fenyin, was appointed military commissioner of the Weisai army, and was promoted to commissioner of the southern court of the palace secretariat together with vice commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 罷，判河陽。

translations.literal: He was dismissed and assigned to administer Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed from those posts, he was assigned to administer Heyang.

sentences.zh: 丁父母憂，起復，徙武寧軍節度使，拜同中書門下平章事、判陳州。

translations.literal: Upon mourning for his parents he was recalled from mourning, transferred to Military Commissioner of the Wuning Army, and appointed Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Administrator of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents died he entered mourning but was recalled to service, transferred to military commissioner of the Wuning army, and appointed co-director of the secretariat-chancellery with charge of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 累遷鎮安軍、淮南節度使、判壽州。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Military Commissioner of the Zhen'an Army and the Huainan Circuit, and Administrator of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively made military commissioner of the Zhen'an army and the Huainan circuit and assigned to administer Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣中書舍人張師德就賜告敕。

translations.literal: The court sent Secretariat Drafter Zhang Shide to bestow upon him an edict of appointment in person.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Secretariat drafter Zhang Shide to deliver his appointment edict in person.

sentences.zh: 尋召為樞密使兼群牧制置使、會靈觀使。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was summoned as Commissioner of Military Affairs, together with Commissioner for Pasturage Administration and Director of the Huiling Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was recalled as commissioner of military affairs, and also made commissioner for pasturage administration and director of the Huiling Temple.

sentences.zh: 先名旻，至是表改名耆。

translations.literal: His original name had been Min; at this time he submitted a memorial to change his name to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He had originally been named Min; at this point he submitted a memorial asking to change his name to Qi.

sentences.zh: 加尚書左僕射，歷河陽、泰寧、山南東道、昭德軍節度使，進兼侍中，封鄧國公。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, served successively as Military Commissioner of Heyang, Taining, the Shannan East Circuit, and the Zhaode Army, was advanced to Palace Attendant as well, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made left vice director of the Imperial Secretariat, served successively as military commissioner of Heyang, Taining, the Shannan East circuit, and the Zhaode army, was promoted to palace attendant as well, and was enfeoffed as duke of Deng.

sentences.zh: 章獻太后崩，以左僕射、護國軍節度出判許州，移襄、鄧、孟、許、陳、壽六州，封徐國公。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Zhangxian died, he went out as Left Vice Director and Military Commissioner of the Huguo Army to administer Xuzhou, was transferred among the six prefectures of Xiang, Deng, Meng, Xu, Chen, and Shou, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Zhangxian died, he left the capital as left vice director and military commissioner of the Huguo army to administer Xuzhou, was transferred among Xiang, Deng, Meng, Xu, Chen, and Shou, and was enfeoffed as duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 耆為人重密，有智數，真宗在東宮，嘗命授以《論語》、《左氏春秋》，後又賜《宸戒》二十條及《聖政記》、《冊府元龜》，故頗知傳記及術數之學，言象緯輒中。

translations.literal: Qi as a man was grave and secretive and possessed stratagem; when Zhenzong was in the Eastern Palace he was once ordered to be taught the Analects and the Zuo Tradition; later he was also granted the twenty articles of Imperial Admonitions, the Record of Sagely Governance, and the Prime Tortoise of the Archive Hall; therefore he was quite versed in historical writing and numerological arts, and when he spoke of celestial signs he often hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was grave, secretive, and shrewd. While Zhenzong was crown prince he had been instructed in the Analects and the Zuo Tradition, and later received the twenty articles of Imperial Admonitions, the Record of Sagely Governance, and the Prime Tortoise of the Archive Hall. He therefore knew historical writing and numerological arts well, and his remarks on celestial signs often proved accurate.

sentences.zh: 章獻太后微時嘗寓其家，耆事之甚謹。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Zhangxian was still obscure she had once lodged in his household, and Qi served her with great care.
translations.idiomatic: In her early days Empress Dowager Zhangxian had once stayed in his home, and Qi had served her with great care.

sentences.zh: 及太后預政，寵遇最厚，賜第尚書省西，凡七百楹，安佚富盛逾四十年。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager took part in government, his favor was the greatest; she granted him a residence west of the Imperial Secretariat, seven hundred bays in all, and he lived in ease and wealth for more than forty years.
translations.idiomatic: Once the empress dowager entered politics, no one was favored more richly than he. She granted him a residence west of the Imperial Secretariat—seven hundred bays in all—and for more than forty years he lived in comfort and wealth.

sentences.zh: 家居為曲闌，積百貨其中，與群婢相貿易。

translations.literal: At home he made a curved market enclosure, piled all sorts of goods within it, and traded with the maidservants.
translations.idiomatic: At home he built a curved market enclosure, stocked it with all sorts of goods, and traded with his maidservants.

sentences.zh: 有病者親為診切，以藥儥之，欲錢不出也。

translations.literal: When someone was ill he personally examined and diagnosed, selling medicine in trade; if they wanted cash he would not dispense it.
translations.idiomatic: When someone fell ill he personally examined the patient and sold medicine by barter—if they wanted to pay in cash, he would not give them any.

sentences.zh: 所歷藩鎮，人頗以為擾。

translations.literal: In the military commissions he passed through, people generally regarded him as a nuisance.
translations.idiomatic: In the regions where he served as military commissioner, people generally found him a nuisance.

sentences.zh: 然御諸子嚴，日一見之，即出就外舍，論者亦以此多之。

translations.literal: Yet he was strict with his sons, seeing each of them once a day and then sending them out to the outer quarters; critics also praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was strict with his sons, seeing each of them once a day before sending them out to the outer quarters, and critics praised him for that as well.

sentences.zh: 以太子太師致仕，卒，贈太師兼侍中，諡榮僖。

translations.literal: He retired as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, died, was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor together with Palace Attendant, and was given the posthumous title Rongxi.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as grand preceptor of the heir apparent and died. He was posthumously granted grand preceptor together with palace attendant, with the posthumous title Rongxi.

sentences.zh: 子二十四人。

translations.literal: He had twenty-four sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had twenty-four sons.

sentences.zh: 得一，慶曆中守貝州，妖人王則作亂，不能死，又與之草禮儀，伏誅；

translations.literal: Deyi, during Qingli, was prefect of Beizhou; when the sorcerer Wang Ze rebelled he failed to die for the cause and even drafted ritual protocols for Wang Ze—he was executed;
translations.idiomatic: Deyi served as prefect of Beizhou during the Qingli era. When the sorcerer Wang Ze rebelled he failed to die in defense of the city and even drafted ritual protocols for Wang Ze; he was executed;

sentences.zh: 可一，坐與群婢賊殺其妻，棄市；

translations.literal: Keyi, for joining with the maidservants in murdering his wife by treachery, was executed in the marketplace;
translations.idiomatic: Keyi was executed in the marketplace for conspiring with the maidservants to murder his wife;

sentences.zh: 利一，團練使；

translations.literal: Liyi, Regimental Commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Liyi became a regimental commissioner;

sentences.zh: 誠一，客省使、樞密都承旨。

translations.literal: Chengyi, Reception Commissioner and Chief Palace Aide of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyi served as reception commissioner and chief palace aide of the bureau of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 子 希一

translations.literal: Son: Xiyi
translations.idiomatic: Son: Xiyi

sentences.zh: 希一，字簡翁，以父耆蔭，累官引進使，在知冀、邢等九州。

translations.literal: Xiyi, styled Jianweng, by his father Qi's yin privilege rose through offices to Introducing Commissioner and served as prefect of nine prefectures including Ji and Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi, courtesy name Jianweng, entered office through his father Qi's privilege and rose to introducing commissioner, serving as prefect of nine prefectures including Ji and Xing.

sentences.zh: 貝州叛，希一先引兵至，得其水門。

translations.literal: When Beizhou rebelled, Xiyi was first to lead troops there and secured its water gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Beizhou rebelled, Xiyi was the first to lead troops there and secured its water gate.

sentences.zh: 猶絓兄得一累，監洪州鹽。

translations.literal: Still impeded by his brother Deyi's crime, he was made overseer of Hongzhou salt.
translations.idiomatic: Still held back by his brother Deyi's disgrace, he was made overseer of salt at Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 復為河北緣邊安撫副使。

translations.literal: He was again made Vice Pacification Commissioner of the Hebei frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made vice pacification commissioner on the Hebei frontier.

sentences.zh: 請徙邊兵內地以寬糴費，每州歲為市平以糴邊穀，使人不能高下其價；

translations.literal: He requested moving frontier troops inland to reduce grain purchase costs; each prefecture was to set an annual fair market price to purchase frontier grain, so people could not arbitrarily raise or lower the price;
translations.idiomatic: He asked that frontier troops be moved inland to reduce grain-purchase costs, and that each prefecture set an annual fair price for buying frontier grain so that no one could manipulate the price;

sentences.zh: 戍卒之孥給糧，先軍士一日，使其家為伍保，坐以逃亡之累，皆著為法。

translations.literal: the families of garrison soldiers were to be given grain rations one day before the soldiers, their households made into mutual-responsibility groups bearing the penalty for desertion—all of which was codified as law.
translations.idiomatic: the families of garrison soldiers were to receive rations one day before the soldiers themselves, their households organized into mutual-responsibility groups liable for desertion, and all of this was written into law.

sentences.zh: 徙成都利州路鈐轄、真定府路總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Controller of the Chengdu-Lizhou Circuit and Overall Commander of the Zhending Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military controller of the Chengdu-Lizhou circuit and overall commander of the Zhending circuit.

sentences.zh: 累使遼及館客，遼人嘗以雄州不當禁漁界河、及役白溝兩屬民為言。

translations.literal: He repeatedly served as envoy to Liao and as host to envoys; the Liao people once complained that Xiongzhou ought not to forbid fishing on the border river and that corvée should not be levied on the dual-jurisdiction people of Baigou.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly served as envoy to Liao and as host to Liao envoys. The Liao once complained that Xiongzhou should not forbid fishing on the border river and that corvée should not be levied on the dual-jurisdiction people of Baigou.

sentences.zh: 希一曰：「界河之禁，起於大國統和年，今文移尚存。

translations.literal: Xiyi said: "The prohibition on the border river began in the Great State's Tonghe era; the documents still exist today.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi said, "The ban on the border river dates to your state's Tonghe era—the documents still exist.

sentences.zh: 白溝本輸中國田租，我太宗特除之，自是大國侵牟立稅，故名兩屬，惡有中國不役之理？

translations.literal: Baigou originally paid land tax to China; our Taizong specially exempted it. Since then the Great State has encroached and imposed taxes, hence the name 'dual jurisdiction'—how could there be any reason China should not levy corvée?"
translations.idiomatic: Baigou originally paid land tax to China, and our Taizong specially exempted it. Since then your state has encroached and imposed taxes, which is why the area is called dual jurisdiction—how could China have no right to levy corvée?"

sentences.zh: 」遼人詞塞。

translations.literal: The Liao people had no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao envoys were left speechless.

sentences.zh: 以均州防禦使提舉集禧觀，卒。

translations.literal: As Defender of Junzhou he was made Director of the Jixi Temple and died.
translations.idiomatic: As defender of Junzhou he was made director of the Jixi Temple and died.

sentences.zh: 弟利一。

translations.literal: Younger brother: Liyi.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Liyi.

sentences.zh: 子 利一

translations.literal: Son: Liyi
translations.idiomatic: Son: Liyi

sentences.zh: 利一，字和叔。

translations.literal: Liyi, styled Heshu.
translations.idiomatic: Liyi, courtesy name Heshu.

sentences.zh: 以蔭補供奉官、光州都監。

translations.literal: By yin privilege he was appointed Attendant and Chief Supervisor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Through yin privilege he was appointed an attendant and chief supervisor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 提點京東、淮南刑獄，知莫、冀二州，為河北緣邊安撫都監兼閤門通事舍人、知廣信軍。

translations.literal: He was made Judicial Intendant of Jingdong and Huainan, Prefect of Mo and Ji, Frontier Pacification Chief Supervisor of Hebei together with Gate Protocol Attendant, and Prefect of the Guangxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judicial intendant for Jingdong and Huainan, prefect of Mo and Ji, chief frontier pacification supervisor of Hebei together with gate protocol attendant, and prefect of the Guangxin army.

sentences.zh: 諜告遼人宋元寇邊，利一置酒高會於譙門，元率眾遁去。

translations.literal: A spy reported that the Liao man Song Yuan was raiding the frontier; Liyi held a grand banquet at the watchtower gate, and Yuan led his men and fled.
translations.idiomatic: A spy reported that the Liao commander Song Yuan was raiding the frontier. Liyi held a grand banquet at the watchtower gate, and Yuan led his men and fled.

sentences.zh: 徙知保州、雄州，累遷西上閤門使、嘉州團練使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as Prefect of Baozhou and Xiongzhou, and was repeatedly promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and Regimental Commissioner of Jiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Baozhou and Xiongzhou, and was successively promoted to western upper gate commissioner and regimental commissioner of Jiazhou.

sentences.zh: 遼人刺兩屬民為兵，民不堪其辱，利一綏來之。

translations.literal: The Liao conscripted dual-jurisdiction people as soldiers; the people could not bear the humiliation; Liyi soothed and drew them in.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao conscripted dual-jurisdiction residents as soldiers, the people could not bear the abuse, and Liyi reassured them and won them over.

sentences.zh: 有大姓舉族南徙，慕而來者至二萬。

translations.literal: One great clan moved south with the whole family; those who came in admiration reached twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: One great clan moved south with its entire household, and those who followed in admiration numbered as many as twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 利一發稟振恤，且移詰涿州，自是不敢復刺。

translations.literal: Liyi issued grain from the stores for relief and also sent a protest to Zhuozhou; from then on they did not dare conscript again.
translations.idiomatic: Liyi opened the granaries for relief and also sent a protest to Zhuozhou; after that the Liao did not dare conscript there again.

sentences.zh: 巡檢趙用有罪，坐不察舉，改衛州鈐轄。

translations.literal: The patrol inspector Zhao Yong committed an offense; for failing to investigate and report it Liyi was transferred to Military Controller of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When patrol inspector Zhao Yong committed an offense, Liyi was punished for failing to investigate and report it and was transferred to military controller of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，為定州路鈐轄，進馬步軍總管，徙真定、大名府路。

translations.literal: After a long time he was made Military Controller of the Dingzhou Circuit, was advanced to Overall Commander of the Horse and Foot Soldiers, and was transferred to the Zhending and Daming circuits.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he became military controller of the Dingzhou circuit, was promoted to overall commander of the horse and foot soldiers, and was transferred to the Zhending and Daming circuits.

sentences.zh: 歷知代、滄、澶、鄭、相州，終雄州團練使。

translations.literal: He successively served as Prefect of Dai, Cang, Chan, Zheng, and Xiang, and ended as Regimental Commissioner of Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as prefect of Dai, Cang, Chan, Zheng, and Xiang, and ended his career as regimental commissioner of Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 楊崇勳

translations.literal: Yang Chongxun
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chongxun

sentences.zh: 楊崇勳，字寶臣，薊州人。

translations.literal: Yang Chongxun, styled Baochen, was a native of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chongxun, courtesy name Baochen, came from Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 祖守斌，事太祖為龍捷指揮使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shoubin served Taizu as commander of the Dragon Swift Army.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shoubin served Taizu as commander of the Dragon Swift army.

sentences.zh: 父全美，事太宗為殿前指揮使。

translations.literal: His father Quanmei served Taizong as commander of the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quanmei served Taizong as commander of the palace front.

sentences.zh: 崇勳以父蔭為東西班承旨，事真宗於東宮。

translations.literal: Chongxun by his father's yin privilege became an attendant of the Eastern and Western Companies and served Zhenzong in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxun entered office through his father's privilege as an attendant of the eastern and western companies and served Zhenzong when he was crown prince.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗曰：「“聞若嗜學，吾授若書。

translations.literal: The Emperor once said: "I hear you are fond of study—I shall teach you books."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said, "I hear you love study—I shall teach you books."

sentences.zh: 」崇勳自是稍通兵法及前代興廢之事。

translations.literal: From then on Chongxun gradually came to understand military methods and the rise and fall of previous dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Chongxun gradually mastered military methods and the rise and fall of earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，遷左侍禁、西頭供奉官、寄班祗候。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong ascended the throne, he was transferred to Left Palace Guard, Western Head Attendant, and Temporary Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong ascended the throne, he was transferred to left palace guard, western head attendant, and temporary gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 雷有終討王均，崇勳承受公事，以奏捷擢內殿崇班。

translations.literal: When Lei Youzhong suppressed Wang Jun, Chongxun handled official business as courier commissioner and was promoted to Inner Palace Attendant for reporting victory.
translations.idiomatic: When Lei Youzhong suppressed Wang Jun, Chongxun served as courier commissioner on the campaign and was promoted to inner palace attendant for reporting the victory.

sentences.zh: 累遷西上閤門使、群牧都監，改副使，以左衛大將軍、恩州刺史為樞密都承旨，尋提舉樞密諸房、通進銀臺司事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and Director of Pasturage, then changed to Vice Director; as Left Guard General and Prefect of Enzhou he became Chief Palace Aide of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and soon afterward oversaw the various offices of the Bureau of Military Affairs and the affairs of the Silver Terrace Forwarding Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively promoted to western upper gate commissioner and director of pasturage, then made vice director; as left guard general and prefect of Enzhou he became chief palace aide of the bureau of military affairs, and soon afterward oversaw the bureau's various offices and the affairs of the Silver Terrace Forwarding Office.

sentences.zh: 以英州防禦使為馬軍都虞候、並代州馬步軍副都總管，留為客省使、領群牧使。

translations.literal: As Defender of Yingzhou he was made Chief Adjutant of the Horse Soldiers and Vice Overall Commander of the Horse and Foot Soldiers of Bingzhou and Daizhou; he remained as Reception Commissioner and headed the Pasturage Commission.
translations.idiomatic: As defender of Yingzhou he was made chief adjutant of the horse soldiers and vice overall commander of the horse and foot soldiers of Bing and Dai, while remaining reception commissioner and head of the pasturage commission.

sentences.zh: 真宗久不豫，寇準罷。

translations.literal: Zhenzong was long indisposed, and Kou Zhun was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong had long been ill, and Kou Zhun was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 入內副都知周懷政謀奉帝為太上皇，傳位太子，復相準。

translations.literal: The Inner Deputy Director Zhou Huaizheng plotted to install the Emperor as Retired Emperor, transfer the throne to the Heir Apparent, and restore Kou Zhun as chief councillor.
translations.idiomatic: The inner deputy director Zhou Huaizheng plotted to make the emperor retired emperor, transfer the throne to the heir apparent, and restore Kou Zhun as chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 嘗以謀訪崇勳，崇勳以變告。

translations.literal: He once consulted Chongxun about the plot, and Chongxun reported the treason.
translations.idiomatic: He once sought Chongxun's counsel on the plot, and Chongxun reported the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 丁謂得其辭，夜造曹利用，共議發之。

translations.literal: Ding Wei obtained his confession, went by night to visit Cao Liyong, and together they discussed exposing the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei obtained his confession, visited Cao Liyong by night, and together they discussed exposing the plot.

sentences.zh: 翌日，誅懷政，擢崇勳鄧州觀察使，不拜，乃以內客省使領桂州觀察使，復兼群牧使。

translations.literal: The next day Huaizheng was executed; Chongxun was promoted to Observation Commissioner of Dengzhou but did not accept the appointment, and so was made Inner Reception Commissioner heading the Observation Commission of Guizhou, again also heading the Pasturage Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Huaizheng was executed. Chongxun was promoted to observation commissioner of Dengzhou but declined the appointment, and was instead made inner reception commissioner with charge of Guizhou, again also heading the pasturage commission.

sentences.zh: 初，群牧置使皆以文臣領之，崇勳曰：「馬者戰備，雖無事，可去邪？」

translations.literal: At first the pasturage commission had always been headed by civil officials; Chongxun said: "Horses are military preparedness—even in peace, can they be dispensed with?"
translations.idiomatic: At first the pasturage commission had always been headed by civil officials. Chongxun said, "Horses are military preparedness—even in peacetime, can they be done away with?"

sentences.zh: 章獻與仁宗言，先帝最稱崇勳質信，可任大事，乃進樞密使。

translations.literal: Zhangxian spoke with Renzong, saying the late emperor had most praised Chongxun's honesty and trustworthiness and that he could be entrusted with great affairs; he was then advanced to Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangxian told Renzong that the late emperor had most praised Chongxun's honesty and trustworthiness and that he could be entrusted with great affairs, and Chongxun was then promoted to commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 百官詣洪福院上章懿冊，退而立班奉慰，宰相張士遜過崇勳園飲，日中期不至。

translations.literal: The hundred officials went to Hongfu Temple to present the memorial tablet of Empress Zhangyi, withdrew, and stood in formation to offer condolences; the chief councillor Zhang Shixun passed by Chongxun's garden to drink, and at midday failed to arrive on time.
translations.idiomatic: When the officials went to Hongfu Temple to present Empress Zhangyi's memorial tablet, withdrew, and stood in formation to offer condolences, chief councillor Zhang Shixun stopped at Chongxun's garden to drink and failed to arrive on time at midday.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞范諷劾奏，與士遜俱罷，以同平章事、河陽三城節度使判許州。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Fan Feng impeached them; both were dismissed; he was made Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Military Commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang with charge of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Fan Feng impeached them, and both were dismissed. Chongxun was made co-director of the secretariat-chancellery and military commissioner of the three cities of Heyang with charge of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 翌日，改陳州。

translations.literal: The next day he was changed to Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day his assignment was changed to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 景祐初，懷政家人訟冤，遂罷同平章事，知壽州，徙亳州，復知陳州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyou, Huaizheng's family petitioned over a miscarriage of justice; he was then dismissed as Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, made Prefect of Shouzhou, transferred to Bozhou, and again made Prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingyou era, Huaizheng's family petitioned that he had been wronged. Chongxun was then dismissed as co-director of the secretariat-chancellery, made prefect of Shouzhou, transferred to Bozhou, and again made prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹將渝盟，朝廷擇將備邊，崇勳請行，復拜同平章事、判定州。

translations.literal: The Khitan were about to break the treaty; the court chose generals to prepare the frontier; Chongxun requested to go; he was again appointed Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Administrator of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan were about to break the treaty, the court chose generals to guard the frontier. Chongxun volunteered to go and was again appointed co-director of the secretariat-chancellery with charge of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 既而老不任事，徙成德軍，又徙鄭州。

translations.literal: Before long, old age made him unfit for office; he was transferred to the Chengde Army, then again to Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long old age left him unfit for duty, and he was transferred to the Chengde army and then to Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 坐其子宗誨納賕枉法，以左衛上將軍致仕，改太子太保，卒。

translations.literal: Because his son Zonghui accepted bribes and perverted the law, he retired as Left Guard Senior General, was changed to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Because his son Zonghui had taken bribes and perverted the law, he retired as left guard senior general, was reassigned as grand preceptor of the heir apparent, and died.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，諡恭密，尋改諡恭毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Commandant, given the posthumous title Gongmi, and soon afterward the posthumous title was changed to Gongyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted grand commandant with the posthumous title Gongmi, which was soon changed to Gongyi.

sentences.zh: 崇勳性貪鄙，久任軍職。

translations.literal: Chongxun by nature was greedy and base and long held military office.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxun was greedy and base by nature and long held military office.

sentences.zh: 當真宗時，每對，輒肆言中外事，喜中傷人，人以是畏之。

translations.literal: During Zhenzong's reign, at every audience he would freely speak of affairs at court and abroad, delighting in slandering others; people therefore feared him.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenzong's reign, at every audience he would speak freely about affairs at court and abroad and delighted in slandering others, so people feared him.

sentences.zh: 在藩鎮日，嘗役兵工作木偶戲人，塗以丹白，舟載鬻於京師。

translations.literal: While serving in military commissions he once forced soldiers to make puppet-theater figures, painted them red and white, and shipped them by boat to sell in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as military commissioner he once forced soldiers to make puppet-theater figures, painted them red and white, and shipped them by boat to sell in the capital.

sentences.zh: 夏守恩

translations.literal: Xia Shouen
translations.idiomatic: Xia Shouen

sentences.zh: 夏守恩，字君殊，幷州榆次人。

translations.literal: Xia Shouen, styled Junshu, was a native of Yuci in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Shouen, courtesy name Junshu, came from Yuci in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父遇，為武騎軍校，與契丹戰，歿。

translations.literal: His father Yu was a corporal of the Martial Cavalry Army; he fought the Khitan and died.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu was a corporal in the Martial Cavalry army; he fought the Khitan and was killed.

sentences.zh: 時守恩才六歲。

translations.literal: At that time Shouen was only six years old.
translations.idiomatic: Shouen was then only six years old.

sentences.zh: 補下班殿侍，給事襄王宮，累遷西頭供奉官。

translations.literal: He was appointed as a lower-rank Hall Attendant, served in the Prince of Xiang's palace, and was promoted through several ranks to Western Head Honored Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a lower-rank hall attendant in the Prince of Xiang's household and rose through several posts to Western Head Honored Attendant.

sentences.zh: 天聖初，加步軍副都指揮使、威塞軍節度使，為永定陵總管。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiansheng, he was additionally made Vice Commander-in-Chief of the Foot Soldiers and Military Commissioner of the Weisai Army, and was made Supervisor-General of the Yongding Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tiansheng era he was further appointed vice commander-in-chief of the foot soldiers and military commissioner of the Weisai army, with charge of the Yongding Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 雷允恭、邢中和徙皇堂，穿地得水泉，土石相半，人疫，功不就。

translations.literal: Lei Yunong and Xing Zhonghe relocated the imperial coffin chamber; digging revealed a spring, earth and stone were evenly mixed, people fell ill with plague, and the work could not be completed.
translations.idiomatic: When Lei Yunong and Xing Zhonghe moved the imperial coffin chamber, their digging struck a spring; earth and stone were intermixed, plague broke out among the workers, and the project failed.

sentences.zh: 守恩以聞，允恭等伏誅。

translations.literal: Shouen reported this; Yunong and the others were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Shouen reported the matter, and Yunong and his associates were put to death.

sentences.zh: 徙節河陽三城，歸本鎮，知澶、相、曹三州，幷代路馬步軍都總管，歷天雄、泰寧、武寧節度使，為真定府定州路都總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to command the Three Cities of Heyang, returned to his home command, served as prefect of Chen, Xiang, and Cao prefectures, was Overall Commander of horse and foot forces on the Bing-Dai Circuit, successively held military commissioner posts of Tianxiong, Taining, and Wuning, and was made Overall Commander of the Zhending Prefecture and Dingzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to command the Three Cities of Heyang, returned to his home command, governed Chen, Xiang, and Cao, served as overall commander of horse and foot forces on the Bing-Dai circuit, held in turn the military commissioner posts of Tianxiong, Taining, and Wuning, and was made overall commander of Zhending prefecture and the Dingzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 守恩所至，恃寵驕恣不法。

translations.literal: Wherever Shouen went, he relied on imperial favor to act arrogantly and lawlessly.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Shouen served, he leaned on imperial favor to behave arrogantly and outside the law.

sentences.zh: 其子元吉通賂遺，市物多不予直。

translations.literal: His son Yuanji gave bribes and gifts; when buying goods he often paid no fair price.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanji trafficked in bribes and gifts, and when buying goods often refused to pay a fair price.

sentences.zh: 定州通判李參發其贓，命侍御史趙及與大名府通判李鉞鞫問得實，法當死，帝命貸之，除名連州編管，卒貶所。

translations.literal: Dingzhou Vice Prefect Li Can exposed his corruption; the emperor ordered Investigating Censor Zhao Ji and Daming Prefecture Vice Prefect Li Yue to interrogate him—the facts were established, and by law he deserved death; the emperor ordered his life spared, stripped him of rank and sent him to Lianzhou under registered exile, and he died in the place of banishment.
