translations.idiomatic: When Dingzhou vice prefect Li Can exposed his corruption, the emperor ordered investigating censor Zhao Ji and Daming vice prefect Li Yue to examine the case; the charges were proved and the law called for death, but the emperor spared his life, stripped him of rank, and sent him into registered exile at Lianzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 弟 守贇

translations.literal: Younger brother: Shouyun
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Shouyun

sentences.zh: 守贇，字子美。

translations.literal: Shouyun, styled Zimei.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyun, courtesy name Zimei.

sentences.zh: 初，守恩給事襄王邸，王問其兄弟，守恩言守贇四歲而孤，日侍王邸，不得時撫養，心輒念之。

translations.literal: Initially Shouen served in the Prince of Xiang's residence. The prince asked about his brothers; Shouen said Shouyun had been orphaned at four, attended the prince's residence every day, and could not be nurtured on time—he always thought of him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouen first served in the Prince of Xiang's household, the prince asked about his brothers. Shouen said that Shouyun had been orphaned at four, spent his days in attendance at the prince's residence, and could not be cared for properly—yet Shouen always had him in mind.

sentences.zh: 王為動容，即日召入宮，而憐其幼，聽就外舍。

translations.literal: The prince was moved; that same day he summoned Shouyun into the palace, but pitying his youth, allowed him to stay in an outer lodging.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was deeply moved and summoned Shouyun into the palace that same day, but pitying his youth allowed him to lodge outside.

sentences.zh: 後二年，復召入，王乳母齊國夫人使傅婢拊視之。

translations.literal: Two years later he was summoned in again; the prince's wet nurse, the Lady of Qi, had a nursemaid watch over him.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was brought in again, and the prince's wet nurse, the Lady of Qi, assigned a nursemaid to look after him.

sentences.zh: 稍長，習通文字。

translations.literal: As he grew somewhat older, he studied and mastered written language.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew a little older, he studied and mastered reading and writing.

sentences.zh: 王為太子，守贇典工作事。

translations.literal: When the prince became heir apparent, Shouyun managed construction affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became heir apparent, Shouyun oversaw construction work.

sentences.zh: 及即位，授右侍禁。

translations.literal: When he acceded to the throne, Shouyun was granted Right Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince ascended the throne, Shouyun was appointed Right Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 李繼遷叛，命使綏、夏伺邊釁，遷西頭供奉官、寄班祗候。

translations.literal: When Li Jiqian rebelled, he was ordered to go to Sui and Xia to watch for frontier provocations; he was promoted to Western Head Honored Attendant and Acting Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jiqian rebelled, he was sent to Sui and Xia to watch for signs of trouble on the frontier and was promoted to Western Head Honored Attendant and acting Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝幸大名，為駕前走馬承受。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Daming, he served as Imperial Escort Mounted Courier.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Daming, he served as mounted courier in the imperial escort.

sentences.zh: 康保裔與賊戰，沒，部曲畏誅，聲言保裔降賊，密詔守贇往察之。

translations.literal: Kang Baoyi fought the enemy and perished; his troops, fearing punishment, claimed Baoyi had surrendered to the enemy; a secret edict ordered Shouyun to go investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Baoyi fought the enemy and was killed; his men, fearing punishment, spread word that he had surrendered, and a secret edict ordered Shouyun to investigate.

sentences.zh: 守贇變服入營中，廉問得狀，還奏稱旨。

translations.literal: Shouyun changed clothes and entered the camp, investigated and learned the facts, returned and memorialized to the emperor's satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyun changed clothes, entered the camp in disguise, learned the truth through inquiry, and on returning reported in a manner that pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 詔恤保裔家，以守贇為真定路走馬承受公事。

translations.literal: An edict granted relief to Baoyi's family; Shouyun was made Commissioner of Mounted Courier Affairs on the Zhending Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted relief to Baoyi's family, and Shouyun was made commissioner of mounted courier affairs on the Zhending circuit.

sentences.zh: 帝幸澶淵及祀汾陰，皆為駕前巡檢，累遷東綾錦副使。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Chanyuan and performed the Fen Yin sacrifice, Shouyun served as Imperial Escort Inspector; he was promoted through several ranks to Vice Commissioner of Eastern Brocade.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's visits to Chanyuan and the Fen Yin sacrifice, he served as inspector in the imperial escort and rose through several ranks to vice commissioner of Eastern Brocade.

sentences.zh: 從幸亳州，命修行宮。

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor to Bozhou, he was ordered to build the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying the emperor to Bozhou, he was ordered to construct the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 轉崇儀使、提舉倉草場。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of Honored Ceremonies and put in charge of the grain and fodder depot.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to commissioner of honored ceremonies and put in charge of the grain and fodder depot.

sentences.zh: 帝甚親信之，遣中使問守贇曰：「欲管軍乎？

translations.literal: The emperor trusted him greatly and sent a palace emissary to ask Shouyun: "Do you wish to command troops?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor trusted him deeply and sent a palace emissary to ask Shouyun, "Do you wish to command troops?

sentences.zh: 為橫行使乎？

translations.literal: Or to serve as a roving envoy?"
translations.idiomatic: Or to serve as a roving envoy?"

sentences.zh: 」守贇曰：「臣得日近冕旒足矣。

translations.literal: Shouyun said: "Your servant need only be near the imperial presence day by day—that is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyun replied, "Your servant need only remain near the imperial presence day by day—that is enough.

sentences.zh: 」尋遷西上閤門使、提舉諸司庫務，以右千牛衛大將軍、昭州刺史為樞密都承旨，兼領三班院。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner, put in charge of the various bureaus' treasury affairs, and with the titles of Senior General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard and Prefect of Zhaozhou made Chief Liaison of the Bureau of Military Affairs, concurrently heading the Three-Rank Court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and put in charge of the various bureaus' treasury affairs; with the titles of senior general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard and prefect of Zhaozhou he was made chief liaison of the Bureau of Military Affairs and concurrently headed the Three-Rank Court.

sentences.zh: 每契丹使至，與楊崇勳迭為館伴副使，凡十餘年。

translations.literal: Whenever Khitan envoys arrived, he and Yang Chongxun alternated as deputy host commissioners—for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Khitan envoys arrived, he and Yang Chongxun alternated as deputy host commissioners for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 擢侍衛親軍步軍都虞候，改馬軍、幷代州都總管。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commandant of the Palace Guard Foot Soldiers, then changed to Commandant of the Horse Soldiers and Overall Commander of Bing and Dai prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commandant of the palace guard foot soldiers, then transferred to commandant of the horse soldiers and overall commander of Bing and Dai.

sentences.zh: 累遷步軍、馬軍殿前副都指揮使，建武、鎮東、保大軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was promoted through several ranks to Vice Commander-in-Chief of the Foot and Horse Soldiers before the Throne Hall, and Military Commissioner of the Jianwu, Zhendong, and Baoda Armies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several ranks to vice commander-in-chief of the foot and horse soldiers before the throne hall and military commissioner of the Jianwu, Zhendong, and Baoda armies.

sentences.zh: 俄以修大內勞，除殿前都指揮使，徙定國軍節度使。

translations.literal: Soon, for his labors in repairing the inner palace, he was made Commander-in-Chief before the Throne Hall and transferred to Military Commissioner of the Dingguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, for his work repairing the inner palace, he was made commander-in-chief before the throne hall and transferred to military commissioner of the Dingguo army.

sentences.zh: 守恩坐贓廢，守贇亦以鎮海軍節度使罷管軍，之本鎮。

translations.literal: Shouen was dismissed for corruption; Shouyun likewise ceased commanding troops as Military Commissioner of the Zhenhai Army and returned to his home command.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouen was dismissed for corruption, Shouyun too was relieved of troop command as military commissioner of the Zhenhai army and returned to his home command.

sentences.zh: 逾年，徙定州路都總管，召知樞密院事。

translations.literal: After a year he was transferred to Overall Commander of the Dingzhou Circuit and summoned to serve as Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was transferred to overall commander of the Dingzhou circuit and summoned to direct the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 既入見，帝問西事，守贇言：「平時小障屯兵馬不及千餘，賊兵盛至，固守不暇，安能出門邪？

translations.literal: After entering audience, the emperor asked about western affairs; Shouyun said: "In normal times small stockades station fewer than a thousand troops; when enemy forces arrive in strength, there is no leisure even to hold firm defense—how could one sally forth?"
translations.idiomatic: After he had been received in audience, the emperor asked about western affairs. Shouyun said, "In normal times the small stockades hold fewer than a thousand troops; when the enemy comes in force there is barely time to hold the walls—how could anyone sally out?"

sentences.zh: 宜併其兵以據衝要，伺便邀擊，功或可成。

translations.literal: One should combine their forces to hold strategic points, watch for opportunity to intercept and strike—success may be possible."
translations.idiomatic: Their forces should be combined to hold the vital points, then wait for a chance to intercept and strike—success may yet be possible."

sentences.zh: 」帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 劉平、石元孫敗，人有以降賊誣告者。

translations.literal: When Liu Ping and Shi Yuansun were defeated, some falsely accused them of surrendering to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Ping and Shi Yuansun were defeated, some people falsely accused them of surrendering to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 守贇頗辨其枉，引康保裔事為質，自請將兵擊賊。

translations.literal: Shouyun argued strongly that they had been wronged, cited the Kang Baoyi affair as proof, and volunteered to lead troops against the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyun argued forcefully that they had been wronged, cited the Kang Baoyi affair as precedent, and volunteered to lead troops against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 換宣徽南院使、陝西馬步軍都總管兼經略、安撫、緣邊招討使，命勾當御藥院張德明、黎用信掌御劍以隨之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Southern Court of the Privy Secretariat, Overall Commander of horse and foot forces in Shaanxi with concurrent frontier pacification, soothing, and border-recruitment commissioner posts; Zhang Deming and Li Yongxin of the Imperial Pharmacy Bureau were ordered to bear the imperial sword and accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to commissioner of the Southern Court of the Privy Secretariat and overall commander of horse and foot forces in Shaanxi, with concurrent posts as frontier pacification, soothing, and border-recruitment commissioner; Zhang Deming and Li Yongxin of the Imperial Pharmacy Bureau were ordered to carry the imperial sword and accompany him.

sentences.zh: 然守贇性庸怯，寡方略，不為士卒所服。

translations.literal: Yet Shouyun was by nature mediocre and timid, lacked strategy, and was not respected by the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shouyun was by nature dull and timid, short on strategy, and not respected by the troops.

sentences.zh: 尋詔駐軍河中，居數月，徙屯鄜州。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered him to station troops at Hezhong; after several months he moved camp to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered him to encamp at Hezhong; after several months he moved his camp to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 其子隨為陝西緣邊招討副使。

translations.literal: His son Sui was made Deputy Recruitment Commissioner on the Shaanxi frontier.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sui was made deputy recruitment commissioner on the Shaanxi frontier.

sentences.zh: 時晏殊、宋綬知樞密院，又召守贇同知院事。

translations.literal: At the time Yan Shu and Song Shou directed the Bureau of Military Affairs; Shouyun was again summoned as Associate Director.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yan Shu and Song Shou directed the Bureau of Military Affairs, and Shouyun was again summoned as associate director.

sentences.zh: 隨卒，守贇請罷，以宣徽南院使、天平軍節度使判澶州，以疾徙相州。

translations.literal: When Sui died, Shouyun requested dismissal; as Commissioner of the Southern Court of the Privy Secretariat and Military Commissioner of the Tianping Army he was assigned to Chenzhou; owing to illness he was transferred to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui died, Shouyun asked to be relieved; as commissioner of the Southern Court of the Privy Secretariat and military commissioner of the Tianping army he was assigned to Chenzhou, then transferred to Xiangzhou because of illness.

sentences.zh: 疾稍平，復為真定府定州等路都總管，未至，徙高陽關，就判瀛州。

translations.literal: When his illness eased somewhat, he was again made Overall Commander of the Zhending Prefecture and Dingzhou Circuit and related routes; before he arrived he was transferred to Gaoyang Pass and assigned to administer Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness eased, he was again made overall commander of Zhending prefecture and the Dingzhou circuit and related routes; before he arrived he was transferred to Gaoyang Pass and assigned to administer Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太尉，諡忠僖。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Grand Commandant; posthumous title Zhongxi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted grand commandant with the posthumous title Zhongxi.

sentences.zh: 子 隨

translations.literal: Son: Sui
translations.idiomatic: Son: Sui

sentences.zh: 元昊反，為鄜延路副都總管。

translations.literal: When Yuanhao rebelled, Sui was made Deputy Overall Commander of the Fuyan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao rebelled, he was made deputy overall commander of the Fuyan circuit.

sentences.zh: 隨本名元亨，與元昊有嫌，因奏改焉。

translations.literal: Sui's original name was Yuanheng; he had a grievance with Yuanhao and therefore memorialized to change it.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's original name was Yuanheng; because he had a grievance with Yuanhao, he memorialized to have it changed.

sentences.zh: 尋徙環慶路，未幾，復還鄜延。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Huanqing Circuit; before long he returned to Fuyan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to the Huanqing circuit, and before long returned to Fuyan.

sentences.zh: 元昊為書及錦袍、銀帶投境上，以遺金明李士彬，且約與同叛。

translations.literal: Yuanhao sent a letter together with a brocade robe and silver belt across the border as gifts for Jinming's Li Shibin, and proposed that they rebel together.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao sent a letter, a brocade robe, and a silver belt across the border as gifts for Li Shibin of Jinming, proposing that they rebel together.

sentences.zh: 候人得之，諸將皆疑士彬，獨隨曰：「此行間爾。

translations.literal: Border scouts seized them; all the generals suspected Shibin, but Sui alone said: "This is simply a stratagem of division.
translations.idiomatic: Border scouts seized the package; all the generals suspected Shibin, but Sui alone said, "This is simply a stratagem to sow division.

sentences.zh: 士彬與羌世仇，若有私約，通贈遺，豈使眾知邪？

translations.literal: Shibin and the Tangut are hereditary enemies—if there were a private pact and gifts exchanged, would they let everyone know?"
translations.idiomatic: Shibin and the Tangut are hereditary enemies—if there were a secret pact and gifts passed between them, would they let everyone know?"

sentences.zh: 」乃召士彬與飲，厚撫之。

translations.literal: He then summoned Shibin to drink with him and treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Shibin to drink with him and treated him warmly.

sentences.zh: 士彬感泣，後數日，果擊賊，斬首獲羊馬自效。

translations.literal: Shibin wept with gratitude; several days later he indeed attacked the enemy, beheaded foes and captured sheep and horses to prove his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Shibin wept with gratitude; several days later he did attack the enemy, beheading foes and capturing sheep and horses to prove his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 及守贇知樞密院事，除耀州觀察使、知亳州。

translations.literal: When Shouyun became Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Sui was made Observation Commissioner of Yaozhou and Prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouyun became director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Sui was made observation commissioner of Yaozhou and prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 劉平、石元孫敗，以隨知河中府。

translations.literal: When Liu Ping and Shi Yuansun were defeated, Sui was made Administrator of Hezhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Ping and Shi Yuansun were defeated, Sui was made administrator of Hezhong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 守贇經略安撫陝西，留領會靈觀事。

translations.literal: Shouyun pacified and soothed Shaanxi; Sui remained in charge of Huiling Temple affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouyun went to pacify and soothe Shaanxi, Sui remained in charge of affairs at Huiling Temple.

sentences.zh: 守贇還，復為陝西副都總管兼緣邊招討副使。

translations.literal: When Shouyun returned, Sui again became Deputy Overall Commander of Shaanxi and Deputy Frontier Recruitment Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouyun returned, Sui again became deputy overall commander of Shaanxi and deputy frontier recruitment commissioner.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朝廷方以邊事委卿，卿毋以父在機密為嫌。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The court is now entrusting you with frontier affairs—do not let it trouble you that your father holds a post in the inner secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The court is now entrusting you with frontier affairs—do not let it trouble you that your father holds a post in the inner secretariat.

sentences.zh: 」時隨已病，次陝州，卒。

translations.literal: Sui was already ill; he stopped at Shaanzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: By then Sui was already ill; he halted at Shaanzhou and died.

sentences.zh: 贈昭信軍節度使，諡莊恪。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Military Commissioner of the Zhaoxin Army; posthumous title Zhuangke.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted military commissioner of the Zhaoxin army with the posthumous title Zhuangke.

sentences.zh: 隨在邊陲無多戰功，然慎重少過。

translations.literal: Sui had no great military achievements on the frontier, yet he was cautious and seldom erred.
translations.idiomatic: Sui won no great victories on the frontier, yet he was cautious and seldom erred.

sentences.zh: 論曰：曹利用投身不測之淵，以口舌啖契丹，使河北七十年無鋒鏑之虞，勳業固偉矣。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Cao Liyong threw himself into depths of unknown peril, used speech to feed the Khitan, and kept Hebei free of the dread of clashing arms for seventy years—his achievements were indeed grand.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Cao Liyong risked his life in that perilous moment and talked the Khitan round with his words, keeping Hebei free of the clash of arms for seventy years—his achievement was truly great.

sentences.zh: 嶺南之戰，亦豈可少哉！

translations.literal: Was his campaign in Lingnan not also indispensable!
translations.idiomatic: Was his campaign in Lingnan not indispensable as well!

sentences.zh: 恃功怙寵，禍萌而弗悟，可悲也已！

translations.literal: Relying on his achievements and sheltering in imperial favor, disaster sprouted yet he did not perceive it—how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Yet relying on his achievements and imperial favor, he failed to see disaster taking root—how lamentable!

sentences.zh: 耆、崇勳二夏奮闒茸，位將相，皆驕侈貪吝，恃私恩，違清議，君子所不取也。

translations.literal: Zhang Qi, Yang Chongxun, and the two Xia rose from obscurity to the rank of general and minister; all were arrogant, extravagant, greedy, and stingy, relied on private favor, and defied public opinion—what a gentleman would not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qi, Yang Chongxun, and the two Xia rose from humble origins to the rank of general and minister, yet all were arrogant, extravagant, greedy, and stingy, relied on private favor, and defied public opinion—conduct no gentleman would approve.

sentences.zh: 狄青，字漢臣，汾州西河人。

translations.literal: Di Qing, styled Hanchen, was a native of Xihe in Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Di Qing, courtesy name Hanchen, came from Xihe in Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 善騎射。

translations.literal: He excelled at horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 初隸騎御馬直，選為散直。

translations.literal: At first he served in the Imperial Horse Guard; he was selected as an unattached guard.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served in the Imperial Horse Guard and was selected as an unattached guard.

sentences.zh: 寶元初，趙元昊反，詔擇衛士從邊，以青為三班差使、殿侍、延州指使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoyuan, Zhao Yuanhao rebelled; an edict chose guards to go to the frontier; Qing was made Three-Rank Envoy, Hall Attendant, and Commandant of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Baoyuan era, when Zhao Yuanhao rebelled, an edict chose guards for the frontier; Qing was made Three-Rank Envoy, hall attendant, and commandant of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時偏將屢為賊敗，士卒多畏怯，青行常為先鋒。

translations.literal: At the time deputy generals were repeatedly defeated by the enemy; soldiers were mostly fearful and timid; Qing on campaign was often in the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy generals were repeatedly defeated, the soldiers were mostly fearful, and on campaign Qing was often in the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 凡四年，前後大小二十五戰，中流矢者八。

translations.literal: In all four years, large and small engagements totaled twenty-five; he was struck by arrows eight times.
translations.idiomatic: Over four years he fought twenty-five engagements large and small and was struck by arrows eight times.

sentences.zh: 破金湯城，略宥州，屠隆密、歲香、毛奴、尚羅、慶七、家口等族，燔積聚數萬，收其帳二千三百，生口五千七百。

translations.literal: He captured Jintang city, raided Youzhou, slaughtered the Longmi, Suixiang, Maonu, Shangluo, Qingqi, Jiakou, and other clans, burned stores numbering in the tens of thousands, seized 2,300 of their tents, and took 5,700 captives.
translations.idiomatic: He took Jintang city, raided Youzhou, slaughtered the Longmi, Suixiang, Maonu, Shangluo, Qingqi, Jiakou, and other clans, burned stores numbering in the tens of thousands, seized 2,300 tents, and took 5,700 captives.

sentences.zh: 又城橋子穀，築招安、豐林、新砦、大郎等堡，皆扼賊要害。

translations.literal: He also fortified Qiaozi Valley and built the forts of Zhao'an, Fenglin, Xinzhai, Dalang, and others—all blocking enemy vital points.
translations.idiomatic: He also fortified Qiaozi Valley and built the forts of Zhao'an, Fenglin, Xinzhai, Dalang, and others, all blocking the enemy's vital points.

sentences.zh: 嘗戰安遠，被創甚，聞寇至，即挺起馳赴，眾爭前為用。

translations.literal: Once fighting at Anyuan, he was severely wounded; hearing the enemy had arrived, he immediately roused himself and rode out; all rushed forward to serve under him.
translations.idiomatic: Once, fighting at Anyuan, he was badly wounded; when he heard the enemy had arrived he roused himself at once and rode out, and all rushed forward to follow him.

sentences.zh: 臨敵被發、帶銅面具，出入賊中，皆披靡莫敢當。

translations.literal: Facing the enemy he wore his hair loose and a bronze mask; passing in and out among the enemy, all scattered before him and none dared stand against him.
translations.idiomatic: Facing the enemy he wore his hair loose and a bronze mask; passing in and out of the enemy ranks, all scattered before him and none dared stand against him.

sentences.zh: 尹洙為經略判官，青以指使見，洙與談兵，善之，薦於經略使韓琦、范仲淹曰：「此良將材也。

translations.literal: Yin Zhu served as frontier pacification aide; Qing met him as commandant; Zhu discussed military affairs with him, was impressed, and recommended him to Frontier Commissioners Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan, saying: "This man has the stuff of a fine general.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhu served as frontier pacification aide; Qing met him in his capacity as commandant. After discussing military affairs with him, Zhu was impressed and recommended him to frontier commissioners Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan, saying, "This man has the makings of a fine general.

sentences.zh: 」二人一見奇之，待遇甚厚。

translations.literal: The two, on first meeting, found him remarkable and treated him with great generosity.
translations.idiomatic: On first meeting him, the two found him remarkable and treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 仲淹以《左氏春秋》授之曰：「將不知古今，匹夫勇爾。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan taught him the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals and said: "A general who knows nothing of past and present is merely a common man's courage.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan taught him the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals and said, "A general who knows nothing of past and present has only a common man's courage.

sentences.zh: 」青折節讀書，悉通秦、漢以來將帥兵法，由是益知名。

translations.literal: Qing bent himself to study; he thoroughly mastered the military methods of generals from Qin and Han onward, and from this became still more renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Qing applied himself to study, mastered the military methods of generals from Qin and Han onward, and from that time became still better known.

sentences.zh: 以功累遷西上閤門副使，擢秦州刺史、涇原路副都總管、經略招討副使，又加捧日天武四廂都指揮使、惠州團練使。

translations.literal: Through merit he was promoted through several ranks to Vice Commissioner of the Western Upper Gate, elevated to Prefect of Qinzhou, Deputy Overall Commander of the Jingyuan Circuit, and Deputy Frontier Pacification and Recruitment Commissioner; he was further made Commander of all four companies of the Sun-Rising Heavenly Martial Guard and Militia Commissioner of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Through merit he rose through several ranks to vice commissioner of the Western Upper Gate, was elevated to prefect of Qinzhou, deputy overall commander of the Jingyuan circuit, and deputy frontier pacification and recruitment commissioner, and was further made commander of all four companies of the Sun-Rising Heavenly Martial Guard and militia commissioner of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 仁宗以青數有戰功，欲召見問以方略，會賊寇渭州，命圖形以進。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong, because Qing had repeatedly won battles, wished to summon him and question him on strategy; just then the enemy raided Weizhou, and he was ordered to send up a portrait.
translations.idiomatic: Because Qing had repeatedly won battles, Emperor Renzong wished to summon him and question him on strategy; just then the enemy raided Weizhou, and he was ordered to send up a portrait instead.

sentences.zh: 元昊稱臣，徙真定路副都總管，歷侍衛步軍殿前都虞候、眉州防禦使，遷步軍副都指揮使、保大安遠二軍節度觀察留後，又遷馬軍副都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Yuanhao submitted as a vassal, Qing was transferred to Deputy Overall Commander of the Zhending Circuit, served successively as Commandant of the Palace Guard Foot Soldiers before the Throne Hall and Defender of Meizhou, was promoted to Vice Commander-in-Chief of the Foot Soldiers and Military Commissioner and Observer of the Baoda and Anyuan Armies with provisional jurisdiction, and was again promoted to Vice Commander-in-Chief of the Horse Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao submitted as a vassal, Qing was transferred to deputy overall commander of the Zhending circuit, served in turn as commandant of the palace guard foot soldiers before the throne hall and defender of Meizhou, was promoted to vice commander-in-chief of the foot soldiers and military commissioner and observer of the Baoda and Anyuan armies with provisional jurisdiction, and was again promoted to vice commander-in-chief of the horse soldiers.

sentences.zh: 青奮行伍，十餘年而貴，是時面涅猶存。

translations.literal: Qing rose from the ranks; within little more than ten years he had risen to eminence—at that time the tattoo on his face still remained.
translations.idiomatic: Qing had risen from the ranks to eminence in little more than ten years, and the tattoo on his face still remained.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗敕青傅藥除字，青指其面曰：「陛下以功擢臣，不問門地，臣所以有今日，由此涅爾，臣願留以勸軍中，不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: The emperor once ordered Qing to apply medicine to remove the characters; Qing pointed to his face and said: "Your Majesty promoted your servant for merit without regard to family standing; the reason your servant has reached today is this tattoo; your servant wishes to keep it to encourage the army—I dare not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once ordered Qing to apply medicine to remove the tattoo; Qing pointed to his face and said, "Your Majesty promoted me for merit without regard to family standing; the reason I have reached today is this tattoo, and I wish to keep it to encourage the army—I dare not obey the edict.

sentences.zh: 」以彰化軍節度使知延州，擢樞密副使。

translations.literal: He was made Military Commissioner of the Zhanghua Army with charge of Yanzhou, and elevated to Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military commissioner of the Zhanghua army with charge of Yanzhou and elevated to vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，廣源州蠻儂智高反，陷邕州，又破沿江九州，圍廣州，嶺外騷動。

translations.literal: In the Huangyou era, the Guangyuanzhou barbarian Nong Zhigao rebelled, took Yongzhou, then broke nine prefectures along the river, besieged Guangzhou, and threw the region beyond the mountains into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huangyou era, the Guangyuanzhou chieftain Nong Zhigao rebelled, took Yongzhou, overran nine prefectures along the river, besieged Guangzhou, and threw the region beyond the mountains into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 楊畋等安撫經制蠻事，師久無功。

translations.literal: Yang Tian and others were sent to pacify and direct affairs among the barbarians; the army was long at war without success.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tian and others were sent to pacify and direct affairs among the barbarians, but the campaign dragged on without success.

sentences.zh: 又命孫沔、余靖為安撫使討賊，仁宗猶以為憂。

translations.literal: Sun Mian and Yu Jing were again appointed pacification commissioners to suppress the rebels; Emperor Renzong still worried.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Mian and Yu Jing were again appointed pacification commissioners to suppress the rebels, yet Emperor Renzong still worried.

sentences.zh: 青上表請行，翌日入對，自言：「臣起行伍，非戰伐無以報國。

translations.literal: Qing submitted a memorial requesting to go; the next day he entered for audience and said himself: "Your servant rose from the ranks; without fighting I have no way to repay the state.
translations.idiomatic: Qing submitted a memorial asking to go; the next day he entered for audience and said, "I rose from the ranks; without fighting I have no way to repay the state.

sentences.zh: 願得蕃落騎數百，益以禁兵，羈賊首致闕下。

translations.literal: I wish to obtain several hundred tribal cavalry, add to them the palace guard, seize the rebel leader, and bring him to the imperial court."
translations.idiomatic: Give me several hundred tribal cavalry and add palace troops, and I will seize the rebel leader and bring him to court."

sentences.zh: 」帝壯其言，遂除宣徽南院使、宣撫荊湖南北路、經制廣南盜賊事，置酒垂拱殿以遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor was heartened by his words; he was then appointed Commissioner of the Southern Court of the Privy Secretariat, Pacification Commissioner of the northern and southern circuits of Jing and Hu, and Director of affairs against bandits in Guangnan; wine was set out in the Chui Gong Hall to send him off.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was heartened by his words and appointed him commissioner of the Southern Court of the Privy Secretariat, pacification commissioner of the northern and southern circuits of Jing and Hu, and director of affairs against bandits in Guangnan; wine was set out in the Chui Gong Hall to send him off.

sentences.zh: 時智高還據邕州，青合孫沔、余靖兵次賓州。

translations.literal: At the time Zhigao still held Yongzhou; Qing joined Sun Mian's and Yu Jing's forces and encamped at Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao still held Yongzhou; Qing joined Sun Mian's and Yu Jing's forces and encamped at Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，蔣偕、張忠皆輕敵敗死，軍聲大沮。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jiang Xie and Zhang Zhong had both underestimated the enemy, been defeated, and died; army morale was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jiang Xie and Zhang Zhong had both underestimated the enemy, been defeated, and died, and army morale was badly shaken.

sentences.zh: 青戒諸將毋妄與賊鬥，聽吾所為。

translations.literal: Qing warned the generals not to engage the enemy rashly, but to follow his lead.
translations.idiomatic: Qing warned the generals not to engage the enemy rashly and to follow his lead.

sentences.zh: 廣西鈐轄陳曙乘青未至，輒以步卒八千犯賊，潰於崑崙關，殿直袁用等皆遁。

translations.literal: Guangxi Military Controller Chen Shu, taking advantage of Qing's not yet having arrived, rashly led eight thousand foot soldiers against the enemy, was routed at Kunlun Pass, and Palatial Aide Yuan Yong and others all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi military controller Chen Shu, before Qing had arrived, rashly led eight thousand foot soldiers against the enemy, was routed at Kunlun Pass, and palatial aide Yuan Yong and others all fled.

sentences.zh: 青曰：「令之不齊，兵所以敗。

translations.literal: Qing said: "When orders are not uniform, that is why armies are defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Qing said, "When orders are not uniform, that is why armies are defeated.

sentences.zh: 」晨會諸將堂上，揖曙起，並召用等三十人，按以敗亡狀，驅出軍門斬之。

translations.literal: At dawn he assembled the generals in the hall, bowed and had Shu rise, also summoned Yong and thirty others, charged them on the grounds of defeat and flight, and drove them out the army gate to be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he assembled the generals in the hall, bowed and had Shu rise, summoned Yong and thirty others as well, charged them with defeat and flight, and had them driven out the army gate and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 沔、靖相顧愕眙，諸將股慄。

translations.literal: Mian and Jing looked at each other in shock and dismay; the generals trembled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Mian and Yu Jing looked at each other in shock; the generals trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 已而頓甲，令軍中休十日。

translations.literal: Then he halted the armor, ordered the army to rest ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Then he halted the march and ordered the army to rest for ten days.

sentences.zh: 覘者還，以為軍未即進。

translations.literal: Scouts returned, thinking the army would not advance immediately.
translations.idiomatic: When scouts returned, they reported that the army did not seem about to advance.

sentences.zh: 青明日乃整軍騎，一晝夜絕昆侖關，出歸仁鋪為陣。

translations.literal: The next day Qing marshaled army and cavalry; in one day and night passed Kunlun Pass, emerged at Guirenpu and formed battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Qing marshaled his forces and in a single day and night crossed Kunlun Pass, emerging at Guirenpu to form battle lines.

sentences.zh: 賊既失險，悉出逆戰。

translations.literal: The bandits having lost their strategic terrain, all came out to meet them in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost their strategic terrain, the rebels came out to meet them in battle.

sentences.zh: 前鋒孫節搏賊死山下，賊氣銳甚，沔等懼失色。

translations.literal: Vanguard Sun Jie fought the bandits and died at the foot of the mountain; the bandits' spirit was very sharp; Mian and the others turned pale with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard Sun Jie fought the rebels and died at the foot of the mountain; the rebels' fighting spirit was fierce, and Sun Mian and the others turned pale with fear.

sentences.zh: 青執白旗麾騎兵，縱左右翼，出賊不意，大敗之，追奔五十里，斬首數千級，其黨黃師宓、儂建中智中及偽官屬死者五十七人，生擒賊五百餘人，智高夜縱火燒城遁去。

translations.literal: Qing took a white flag and directed the cavalry, unleashed the left and right wings, caught the bandits unawares, routed them greatly, pursued the fleeing enemy fifty li, beheaded several thousand, among his followers Huang Shimi, Nong Jianzhong, Zhizhong and false officials fifty-seven died, captured over five hundred bandits alive, Zhigao at night set fire to the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Qing raised a white flag to direct the cavalry, sent the left and right wings forward, caught the rebels by surprise, and routed them completely. He pursued the fleeing enemy fifty li, beheaded several thousand, and among the dead were fifty-seven of Zhigao's followers Huang Shimi, Nong Jianzhong, and Zhizhong along with appointed officials. Over five hundred rebels were captured alive. That night Zhigao set fire to the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 遲明，青按兵入城，獲金帛钜萬、雜畜數千，招復老壯七千二百嘗為賊所俘脅者，慰遣之。

translations.literal: At dawn, Qing restrained the troops and entered the city, seized gold and silk numbering in the tens of thousands and miscellaneous livestock in the thousands, recalled seven thousand two hundred old and young who had once been captured and coerced by the bandits, comforted and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Qing restrained his troops and entered the city. He seized gold and silk numbering in the tens of thousands and livestock in the thousands, recalled seven thousand two hundred men and youths who had once been captured and coerced by the rebels, comforted them, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 梟黃師宓等邕州城下，斂屍築京觀於城北隅。

translations.literal: Displayed the heads of Huang Shimi and others beneath Yongzhou city, gathered corpses and built a victory mound at the city's northwest corner.
translations.idiomatic: He displayed the heads of Huang Shimi and others beneath Yongzhou, gathered the corpses, and built a victory mound at the northwest corner of the city.

sentences.zh: 時賊屍有衣金龍衣者，眾謂智高已死，欲以上聞。

translations.literal: At the time among the bandit corpses was one clothed in a golden dragon robe; the crowd thought Zhigao was already dead and wished to report it upward.
translations.idiomatic: Among the rebel dead was a body dressed in a golden dragon robe; everyone thought Zhigao was dead and wanted to report it to the court.

sentences.zh: 青曰：「安知非詐邪？

translations.literal: Qing said: "How do we know it is not a deception?"
translations.idiomatic: Qing said, "How do we know this is not a deception?"

sentences.zh: 寧失智高，不敢誣朝廷以貪功也。

translations.literal: Better to miss Zhigao than dare deceive the court to claim merit.
translations.idiomatic: Better to let Zhigao escape than deceive the court to claim credit.

sentences.zh: 」初，青之至邕也，會瘴霧昏塞，或謂賊毒水上流，士飲者多死，青殊憂之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qing reached Yong, miasma and fog choked the air; some said the bandits had poisoned the upstream water and many soldiers died from drinking; Qing was deeply worried.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Qing reached Yongzhou, miasma and fog choked the air. Some said the rebels had poisoned the upstream water and many soldiers died from drinking; Qing was deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 一夕，有泉湧砦下，汲之甘，眾遂以濟。

translations.literal: One night a spring gushed beneath the stockade; drawn, it was sweet; the crowd was thus saved.
translations.idiomatic: One night a spring gushed beneath the stockade; the water drawn from it was sweet, and the army was saved.

sentences.zh: 復為樞密副使，遷護國軍節度使、河中尹。

translations.literal: Again made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, transferred to Military Governor of the Huguo Army and Governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and transferred to military governor of the Huguo Army and governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 還至京師，帝嘉其功，拜樞密使，賜第敦教坊，優進諸子官秩。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, the emperor praised his merit, appointed him Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, granted a mansion in Dunjiao Lane, and advanced the rank of his sons with special favor.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to the capital, the emperor praised his achievement, appointed him commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, granted him a mansion in Dunjiao Lane, and generously advanced the rank of his sons.

sentences.zh: 初，青既行，帝每憂之曰：「青有威名，賊當畏其來。

translations.literal: Earlier, once Qing had departed, the emperor often worried and said: "Qing has a fearsome reputation; the bandits should fear his coming."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Qing had departed, the emperor often expressed concern, saying, "Qing has a fearsome reputation; the rebels should fear his coming.

sentences.zh: 左右使令，非青親信者不可；

translations.literal: Attendants and orders—none but Qing's trusted men may serve.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants and orders—none but his trusted men may serve;

sentences.zh: 雖飲食臥起，皆宜防竊發。

translations.literal: Even in eating, drinking, lying down, and rising, all should guard against sudden attack.
translations.idiomatic: even in eating, drinking, lying down, and rising, he must guard against sudden attack.

sentences.zh: 」乃馳使戒之。

translations.literal: Messengers were dispatched at speed to warn him.
translations.idiomatic: He then dispatched messengers at speed to warn him.

sentences.zh: 及聞青已破賊，顧宰相曰：「速議賞，緩則不足以勸矣。」

translations.literal: When he heard Qing had already defeated the bandits, he turned to the chief ministers and said: "Quickly deliberate rewards; delay will not suffice to encourage others."
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Qing had already defeated the rebels, he turned to the chief ministers and said, "Deliberate rewards at once—delay will not be enough to encourage others."

sentences.zh: 始，交阯願出兵助討智高，余靖言其可信，具萬人糧於邕、欽待之。

translations.literal: At the outset Jiaozhi was willing to send troops to help suppress Zhigao; Yu Jing said they were trustworthy and prepared rations for ten thousand men at Yong and Qin to await them.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset Jiaozhi had offered troops to help suppress Zhigao; Yu Jing said they were trustworthy and prepared rations for ten thousand men at Yong and Qin to await them.

sentences.zh: 詔以緡錢三萬賜交阯為兵費，許賊平厚賞之。

translations.literal: An edict granted Jiaozhi thirty thousand strings of cash as military expenses and promised rich rewards once the bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted Jiaozhi thirty thousand strings of cash as military expenses and promised rich rewards once the rebels were pacified.

sentences.zh: 青既至，檄余靖無通使假兵，即上奏曰：「李德政聲言將步兵五萬、騎一千赴援，非其情實。

translations.literal: Once Qing arrived, he sent a dispatch to Yu Jing forbidding envoys and borrowed troops, then memorialized: "Li Dezheng claims he will send fifty thousand infantry and one thousand cavalry to aid us; this is not his true intent."
translations.idiomatic: Once Qing arrived, he dispatched Yu Jing forbidding envoys and borrowed troops, then memorialized, "Li Dezheng claims he will send fifty thousand infantry and one thousand cavalry to our aid, but this is not his true intent.

sentences.zh: 且假兵於外以除內寇，非我利也。

translations.literal: Moreover, borrowing troops from abroad to suppress internal bandits is not to our advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, borrowing foreign troops to suppress internal rebels is not to our advantage.

sentences.zh: 以一智高而橫蹂二廣，力不能討，乃假兵蠻夷，蠻夷貪得忘義，因而啟亂，何以禦之？

translations.literal: Because of one Zhigao rampaging across the two Guang regions, unable to suppress him by force, to borrow troops from barbarians—the barbarians are greedy for gain and forget righteousness; thus inciting rebellion, how could we repel them?
translations.idiomatic: That one Zhigao could rampage across the two Guang regions, and that we could not suppress him, does not justify borrowing troops from barbarians. Barbarians are greedy for gain and forget righteousness; if we stir them to rebellion, how could we repel them?

sentences.zh: 請罷交阯助兵。

translations.literal: Request to cancel Jiaozhi's aid troops.
translations.idiomatic: I request that Jiaozhi's auxiliary troops be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 賊平，人服其有遠略。

translations.literal: Once the bandits were pacified, people admired his far-reaching strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebels were pacified, people admired his far-reaching strategy.

sentences.zh: 青在樞密四年，每出，士卒輒指目以相矜誇。

translations.literal: Qing was at the Bureau of Military Affairs four years; each time he went out, soldiers would point and gaze at him in mutual boasting.
translations.idiomatic: Qing served at the Bureau of Military Affairs for four years; whenever he went out, soldiers would point and gaze at him with pride.

sentences.zh: 又言者以青家狗生角，且數有光怪，請出青於外以保全之，不報。

translations.literal: Moreover memorialists cited that a dog in Qing's house grew horns and strange lights appeared repeatedly, and asked to transfer Qing outside to preserve him; no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists also cited that a dog in Qing's house had grown horns and strange lights had appeared repeatedly, and asked that Qing be transferred outside the capital to preserve him; no response was given.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，京師大水，青避水徙家相國寺，行止殿上，人情頗疑，乃罷青為同中書門下平章事，出判陳州。

translations.literal: In the Jiayou era, the capital flooded heavily; Qing moved his household to the Xiangguo Temple to escape the water and walked on the hall platform; public sentiment was quite suspicious; Qing was then removed as co-administrator of the Chancellery and dispatched to Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiayou era, when the capital was badly flooded, Qing moved his household to Xiangguo Temple to escape the water and walked on the hall platform; public sentiment turned suspicious, and he was removed as co-administrator of the chancellery and dispatched to serve in Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，疽發髭，卒。

translations.literal: The next year in the second month, a carbuncle erupted at his beard and he died.
translations.idiomatic: The following second month a carbuncle erupted at his beard and he died.

sentences.zh: 帝發哀，贈中書令，諡武襄。

translations.literal: The emperor expressed mourning, posthumously appointed him Chief Minister of the Central Secretariat, posthumous title Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him, posthumously appointed him chief minister of the Central Secretariat, and gave him the posthumous title Wuxiang.

sentences.zh: 青為人慎密寡言，其計事必審中機會而後發。

translations.literal: Qing as a man was cautious, secretive, and sparing of words; in planning affairs he always carefully gauged the opportune moment before acting.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was cautious, discreet, and sparing of words; in planning he always carefully judged the right moment before acting.

sentences.zh: 行師先正部伍，明賞罰，與士同饑寒勞苦，雖敵猝犯之，無一士敢後先者，故其出常有功。

translations.literal: On campaign he first set right the formations, made rewards and punishments clear, shared hunger, cold, labor, and hardship with the soldiers; even when the enemy suddenly attacked, not one soldier dared hang back or rush ahead; therefore his campaigns usually succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he first set the ranks in order, made rewards and punishments clear, and shared hunger, cold, labor, and hardship with his men. Even when the enemy attacked suddenly, not one soldier dared hang back or rush ahead, and therefore his campaigns usually succeeded.

sentences.zh: 尤喜推功與將佐。

translations.literal: He especially liked to credit his achievements to his officers.
translations.idiomatic: He especially liked to give credit to his officers.

sentences.zh: 始，與孫沔破賊，謀一出青，賊既平，經制餘事，悉以諉沔，退若不用意者。

translations.literal: At the outset, breaking the bandits with Sun Mian—the plans all came from Qing; once the bandits were pacified, all follow-up arrangements were shifted onto Mian; he withdrew as if unconcerned.
translations.idiomatic: When he and Sun Mian defeated the rebels, the plans had all come from Qing; once the rebels were pacified, he shifted all follow-up arrangements onto Mian and withdrew as if unconcerned.

sentences.zh: 沔始歎其勇，既而服其為人，自以為不如也。

translations.literal: Mian at first sighed at his bravery; afterward came to admire his character and considered himself inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Mian at first admired his bravery; afterward he came to admire his character and considered himself inferior.

sentences.zh: 尹洙以貶死，青悉力賙其家事。

translations.literal: Yin Zhu died in exile; Qing exerted all his strength to support his family's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Zhu died in exile, Qing exerted himself to support his family's affairs.

sentences.zh: 子諮、詠，並為閤門使。

translations.literal: His sons Zi and Yong both served as Gate Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zi and Yong both served as gate attendants.

sentences.zh: 詠數有戰功。

translations.literal: Yong repeatedly had military achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Yong won military distinction on several occasions.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元年，神宗考次近世將帥，以青起行伍而名動夷夏，深沈有智略，能以畏慎保全終始，慨然思之，命取青畫像入禁中，御製祭文，遣使齎中牢祠其家。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xining, Emperor Shenzong reviewed recent generals; because Qing rose from the ranks yet his name shook Chinese and barbarians, was deep and reserved with strategy, and could through caution and fear preserve himself from beginning to end, he thought of him with emotion, ordered Qing's portrait taken into the forbidden precincts, composed a sacrificial text himself, and sent envoys bearing sacrificial offerings to sacrifice at his home.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xining era, Emperor Shenzong reviewed recent generals. Because Qing had risen from the ranks yet his name resounded among Chinese and barbarians alike, because he was deep and reserved with strategy and could through caution preserve himself from beginning to end, the emperor thought of him with emotion, ordered his portrait taken into the inner palace, composed a sacrificial text himself, and sent envoys bearing sacrificial offerings to sacrifice at his home.

translations.literal: 〈Supplement.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Supplementary Biographies〉

sentences.zh: 張玉 孫節

translations.literal: Zhang Yu; Sun Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu; Sun Jie

sentences.zh: 張玉，字寶臣，保定人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yu, styled Bao Chen, was a native of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu, courtesy name Bao Chen, came from Baoding.

sentences.zh: 以六班散直隸狄青麾下，築青澗、招安砦。

translations.literal: As a Sixth-Rank Unattached Guard he served under Di Qing and built Qingjian and Zhao'an stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as a sixth-rank unattached guard under Di Qing, he built the Qingjian and Zhao'an stockades.

sentences.zh: 遇夏兵三萬，有馳鐵騎挑戰者，玉單持鐵簡出鬥，取其首及馬，軍中因號曰張鐵簡。

translations.literal: Encountering thirty thousand Xia troops, one who charged on iron cavalry to challenge—Yu alone took an iron mace and went out to fight, took his head and horse; the army therefore called him Iron-Mace Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: When they encountered thirty thousand Xia troops, one enemy charged out on iron-armored cavalry to challenge them. Yu alone took an iron mace and fought him, taking his head and horse; the army thereafter called him Iron-Mace Zhang.

sentences.zh: 以狀聞。

translations.literal: The account was reported.
translations.idiomatic: The account was reported to the court.

sentences.zh: 仁宗曰：「真勇將也。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong said: "A truly brave general."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong said, "A truly brave general.

sentences.zh: 」以為本路同巡檢。

translations.literal: He was made co-inspector of this circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was made co-inspector of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 從征儂智高，抵歸仁驛，賊列三銳陳以逆官軍，軍小卻，玉率右廂突騎橫貫賊壘，賊大潰。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Nong Zhigao, arriving at Guiren post station, the bandits arrayed three sharp formations to oppose the government army; the army slightly fell back; Yu led the right wing shock cavalry straight through the bandit camps; the bandits routed completely.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Nong Zhigao, at Guiren post station the rebels formed three sharp battle lines to oppose the government army. When the army fell back slightly, Yu led the right-wing shock cavalry straight through the rebel camps and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 帝召見，使作銳陳於殿廷下，觀破賊之勢。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him for audience, had him form a sharp formation below the hall courtyard, and watched the manner of breaking the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him for audience and had him demonstrate a sharp formation below the hall courtyard to show how he had broken the rebels.

sentences.zh: 擢為廣西鈐轄，徙大名，進龍、神四廂都指揮使，為副都總管。

translations.literal: Promoted to Guangxi Military Controller, transferred to Daming, advanced to Commander of the four Dragon and Divine wings, made Deputy Chief General.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Guangxi military controller, transferred to Daming, advanced to commander of the four Dragon and Divine wings, and made deputy chief general.

sentences.zh: 諒祚攻大順城，玉以兵三千夜擊之，驚潰而去。

translations.literal: Liangzuo attacked Dashun city; Yu with three thousand troops struck at night; startled, they routed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Liangzuo attacked Dashun city, Yu struck at night with three thousand troops and routed them in panic.

sentences.zh: 累遷昭州防禦使，徙涇原。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Defender of Zhaozhou, transferred to Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to defender of Zhaozhou and transferred to Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，慶州卒叛，玉襲逐於石門，卒窮蹙請降，玉斬二百人，坐奪職，降為陵州團練使，居數月，復之。

translations.literal: In the Xining era, Qingzhou soldiers rebelled; Yu pursued them at Shimen; the soldiers, pressed to extremity, requested surrender; Yu beheaded two hundred; on that account lost his post, demoted to Regimental Commander of Lingzhou; after several months, restored.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining era, when Qingzhou soldiers rebelled, Yu pursued them at Shimen. When the rebels, pressed to extremity, requested surrender, he beheaded two hundred of them and was stripped of his post and demoted to regimental commander of Lingzhou; after several months he was restored.

sentences.zh: 王韶開熙河，玉遷宣州觀察使，為副都總管。

translations.literal: Wang Shao opened Xihe; Yu was transferred to Observer of Xuanzhou and made Deputy Chief General.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shao opened Xihe, Yu was transferred to observer of Xuanzhou and made deputy chief general.

sentences.zh: 河北置三十七將，以玉為第一將。

translations.literal: Hebei established thirty-seven generals; Yu was made the first general.
translations.idiomatic: When thirty-seven generals were established in Hebei, Yu was made the first.

sentences.zh: 入為馬步軍都虞候，卒，贈建雄留後。

translations.literal: Entered the capital as Chief Adjutant of Horse and Foot Armies; died; posthumously granted Jianxiong Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as chief adjutant of the horse and foot armies, died, and was posthumously granted the title of Jianxiong military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 孫節，開封人。

translations.literal: Sun Jie, a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jie came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 少隸軍籍，以才勇補右侍禁。

translations.literal: In youth enrolled in military registers; for talent and bravery supplemented as Right Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he entered the military registers and for talent and bravery was appointed a right palace guard.

sentences.zh: 與狄青同在延州，數攻破敵砦有功，累遷西京左藏庫副使。

translations.literal: With Di Qing he was together at Yanzhou; repeatedly captured enemy stockades with merit; repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Western Capital Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He served with Di Qing at Yanzhou, repeatedly captured enemy stockades with distinction, and was promoted to vice director of the Western Capital Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 及青討智高，辟隸麾下。

translations.literal: When Qing campaigned against Zhigao, he was recruited to serve under his banner.
translations.idiomatic: When Qing campaigned against Zhigao, he was recruited to serve under his command.

sentences.zh: 至歸仁鋪，節為前鋒，直前搏戰，賊銳甚，節鏖山下，俄中槍而沒。

translations.literal: Arriving at Guirenpu, Jie was vanguard, went straight forward to fight; the bandits were very sharp; Jie battled at the foot of the mountain; soon struck by a spear and perished.
translations.idiomatic: At Guirenpu he served as vanguard and fought straight ahead. The rebels' fighting spirit was fierce; Jie battled at the foot of the mountain until he was soon struck by a spear and killed.

sentences.zh: 特贈忠武軍節度留後，封其妻為仁壽郡君，官其子二人、從子三人，給諸司副使俸，終其喪。

translations.literal: Specially granted Military Commissioner of Zhongwu Army; enfeoffed his wife as Lady of Renshou Commandery; appointed his two sons and three nephews to office; granted vice-director salaries of various bureaus through the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially granted the title of Zhongwu military commissioner, his wife was enfeoffed as Lady of Renshou Commandery, his two sons and three nephews were given office, and vice-director salaries were granted through the mourning period.

sentences.zh: Disambig.svg参见：檢校司空左武衛上將軍郭公墓誌銘

translations.literal: See also: Epitaph for General Guo, Acting Minister of Works and General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: See also: Epitaph for General Guo, Acting Minister of Works and General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard

sentences.zh: 郭逵，字仲通，其先自邢徙洛。

translations.literal: Guo Kui, styled Zhongtong; his ancestors moved from Xing to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Kui, courtesy name Zhongtong; his ancestors moved from Xing to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 康定中，兄遵死於敵，錄逵為三班奉職，隸陝西范仲淹麾下。

translations.literal: In the Kangding era, elder brother Zun died fighting the enemy; Kui was enrolled as Third-Rank Attendant and placed under Fan Zhongyan in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangding era, when his elder brother Zun died fighting the enemy, Kui was enrolled as a third-rank attendant and placed under Fan Zhongyan in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 仲淹勉以問學。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan encouraged him in study.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan encouraged him to pursue learning.

sentences.zh: 延安清剛社募兵誤殺熟羌，將論死，逵請而免之，活壯士十三人。

translations.literal: At Yan'an, Qinggang Society conscript soldiers mistakenly killed assimilated Qiang; they were to be sentenced to death; Kui pleaded and secured their release, saving thirteen stalwart men.
translations.idiomatic: At Yan'an, Qinggang Society conscripts mistakenly killed assimilated Qiang and were to be sentenced to death; Kui pleaded for them and secured their release, saving thirteen stalwart men.

sentences.zh: 方議取靈武，逵曰：「地遠而食不繼，城大而兵不多，未見其利。

translations.literal: Just as taking Lingwu was under discussion, Kui said: "The land is distant and supplies cannot follow; the city is large and troops are not many; the advantage is not evident."
translations.idiomatic: Just as taking Lingwu was under discussion, Kui said, "The land is distant and supplies cannot follow, the city is large and troops are few—I see no advantage in it.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，涇原任福以全軍沒，人服其先見。

translations.literal: Before long, Ren Fu of Jingyuan lost his entire army; people admired his foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ren Fu of Jingyuan lost his entire army, and people admired Kui's foresight.

sentences.zh: 陳執中安撫京東，奏為駐泊將。

translations.literal: Chen Zhizhong pacified Jingdong; memorialized to make him Garrison General.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Zhizhong was pacification commissioner of Jingdong, he memorialized to appoint Kui a garrison general.

sentences.zh: 執中與賓佐論當今名將，共推葛懷敏。

translations.literal: Zhizhong with his guests and aides discussed today's famous generals; together they promoted Ge Huaimin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong and his staff discussed the famous generals of the day and together praised Ge Huaimin.

sentences.zh: 逵曰：「懷敏易與爾，他日必敗朝廷事。

translations.literal: Kui said: "Huaimin is easy to deal with, but one day he will surely ruin the court's affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Kui said, "Huaimin is easy to deal with, but one day he will surely ruin the court's affairs.

sentences.zh: 」執中始怒，居數日，問曰：「君何以知葛懷敏非名將而敗事邪？

translations.literal: Zhizhong at first grew angry; after several days asked: "How do you know Ge Huaimin is not a famous general and will ruin affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong was angry at first, but after several days asked, "How do you know Ge Huaimin is not a famous general and will ruin affairs?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「喜功徼幸，徒勇無謀，可禽也。

translations.literal: He said: "He loves achievement and seeks lucky chances; merely brave without strategy; he can be captured."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "He loves achievement and seeks lucky chances, is merely brave without strategy—he can be captured.

sentences.zh: 」執中歎曰：「君真知兵，懷敏既覆師矣。

translations.literal: Zhizhong sighed: "You truly know war; Huaimin has already lost his army."
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong sighed and said, "You truly know war—Huaimin has already lost his army.

sentences.zh: 」為真定兵馬監押。

translations.literal: He was made Military Supervisor of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military supervisor of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 保州卒叛，田況遣逵往招之。

translations.literal: Baozhou soldiers rebelled; Tian Kuang sent Kui to summon them.
translations.idiomatic: When Baozhou soldiers rebelled, Tian Kuang sent Kui to negotiate their surrender.

sentences.zh: 逵與亂者侍其臻嘗同事范仲淹，馳至城下，示以舊所佩紫囊。

translations.literal: Kui and the rebel Shiqi Zhen had once served together under Fan Zhongyan; he galloped to beneath the city wall and showed the purple pouch he once wore.
translations.idiomatic: Kui and the rebel leader Shiqi Zhen had once served together under Fan Zhongyan; he galloped to the foot of the city wall and showed the purple pouch he had once worn.

sentences.zh: 臻識之，即與其黨韋貴、史克順皆再拜，邀逵登城。

translations.literal: Zhen recognized it; immediately with his fellows Wei Gui and Shi Keshun all bowed twice and invited Kui to ascend the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen recognized it; he and his followers Wei Gui and Shi Keshun all bowed and invited Kui to ascend the wall.

sentences.zh: 既見，申諭禍福，眾或疑不即下，曰：「“若降，恐不免。

translations.literal: Once they met, he explained blessing and disaster; some doubted and would not immediately surrender, saying: "If we surrender, we fear we will not be spared."
translations.idiomatic: Once they met, he explained the consequences of their choices. Some hesitated to surrender, saying, "If we surrender, we fear we will not be spared.

sentences.zh: 」逵請以身為質，於是開城降。

translations.literal: Kui asked to serve as hostage himself; thereupon they opened the city and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Kui offered himself as hostage, and thereupon they opened the city and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 論功加閤門祗候、環慶兵馬都監。

translations.literal: For merit he was added as Gate Attendant and Military Supervisor of Huanqing.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievement he was promoted to gate attendant and military supervisor of Huanqing.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，不得解官，凡三請乃許。

translations.literal: Encountering mourning for his mother, he could not leave office; after three requests it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he was not permitted to leave office; only after three requests was he allowed to do so.

sentences.zh: 慶帥杜杞贐以錢四十萬，謝弗受。

translations.literal: Du Qi, military governor of Qing, sent a funeral gift of four hundred thousand cash; he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Du Qi, military governor of Qing, sent a funeral gift of four hundred thousand cash; he politely declined.

sentences.zh: 卒喪，為涇原都監。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was made Military Supervisor of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he was made military supervisor of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 拔古渭城，轉通事舍人，徙河北緣邊安撫都監。

translations.literal: Captured Guwei city; transferred to Diplomatic Attendant; moved to Frontier Pacification Military Supervisor of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Guwei city, was transferred to diplomatic attendant, and moved to frontier pacification military supervisor of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 副吳奎使契丹，值其主受尊號，入觀禮。

translations.literal: As deputy to Wu Kui on mission to Khitan; it happened their ruler received an honorific title; entered to observe the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: As deputy to Wu Kui on a mission to the Khitan, he happened to arrive when their ruler received an honorific title and entered to observe the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 使還，黜為汾州都監。

translations.literal: On return from mission, demoted to Military Supervisor of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On his return from the mission he was demoted to military supervisor of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 龐籍鎮河東，俾權忻州。

translations.literal: Pang Ji governed Hedong; had him act as Prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Pang Ji governed Hedong, he had Kui act as prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹來求天池廟地，籍不能決，以諉逵。

translations.literal: Khitan came seeking Tiantci Temple land; Ji could not decide and shifted responsibility to Kui.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan came seeking Tiantci Temple land, Ji could not decide and shifted responsibility to Kui.

sentences.zh: 逵訪得太平興國中故牘，證為王土，檄報之，契丹愧伏。

translations.literal: Kui searched and found old documents from the Taiping Xingguo era proving it as royal territory; replied by dispatch; Khitan submitted in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Kui searched out old documents from the Taiping Xingguo era proving it was imperial territory, replied by dispatch, and the Khitan submitted in shame.

sentences.zh: 湖北溪蠻彭仕羲叛，加帶禦器械，為路鈐轄兼知澧州。

translations.literal: Hubei stream barbarian Peng Shiyi rebelled; added Master of Imperial Armaments, made Circuit Military Controller and concurrently Prefect of Li.
translations.idiomatic: When the stream barbarians of Hubei rebelled under Peng Shiyi, he was given the title Master of Imperial Armaments and made circuit military controller and concurrently prefect of Li.

sentences.zh: 得蠻親信為鄉導，盡平諸隘，遂破其所居桃花州，仕羲棄城走，眾悉降。

translations.literal: Obtained a barbarian trusted man as guide; fully pacified all passes; then broke his residence Taohua prefecture; Shiyi abandoned the city and fled; the masses all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: With a trusted barbarian as guide he pacified all the passes, broke Peng Shiyi's stronghold at Taohua Prefecture, Shiyi abandoned the city and fled, and all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 遷禮賓使，徙南路鈐轄、知邵州。

translations.literal: Transferred to Commissioner of Ceremonial Reception; moved to Southern Route Military Controller and Prefect of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to commissioner of ceremonial reception, moved to southern route military controller, and made prefect of Shao.

sentences.zh: 武岡蠻反，逵討平之。

translations.literal: Wugang barbarians rebelled; Kui suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wugang barbarians rebelled, Kui suppressed and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 累遷容州觀察使。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Observer of Rongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to observer of Rongzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁宗山陵，以逵掌宿衛。

translations.literal: At Emperor Renzong's mountain tomb, Kui was put in charge of night guard.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Renzong's mausoleum, Kui was placed in charge of the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 遷殿前都虞候，出為涇原路副都部署。

translations.literal: Promoted to Chief Adjutant of the Palace Front; sent out as Deputy Chief Deployer of Jingyuan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief adjutant of the Palace Front, then sent out as deputy chief deployer of Jingyuan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 治平二年，以檢校太保同簽書樞密院，旋出領陝西宣撫使，判渭州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiping, as Honorary Grand Guardian he concurrently signed the Bureau of Military Affairs; shortly after went out to lead as Shaanxi Pacification Commissioner, administering Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhiping era he was appointed honorary grand guardian and concurrent signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then soon sent out to serve as Shaanxi pacification commissioner and administrator of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 逵雖立軍功，而驟躋政地，議者不厭，諫官、御史交論之，不聽。

translations.literal: Though Kui had achieved military merit, he had suddenly risen to political rank; those who discussed the matter were displeased; remonstrating officials and censors alternately criticized this; the emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Though Kui had earned military distinction, his sudden leap into high political office displeased the court. Remonstrating officials and censors attacked the appointment in turn, but the emperor would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，遷靜難軍留後，召還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong acceded, Kui was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Jingnan Army and recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong acceded to the throne, Kui was transferred to military commissioner of the Jingnan Army and recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 言者復力爭，乃改宣徽南院使、判鄆州。

translations.literal: Critics again struggled forcefully; thereupon he was changed to Commissioner of the Southern Court of the Privy Pavilion, administering Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Critics again fought the appointment fiercely, and he was instead made commissioner of the Southern Court of the Privy Pavilion and administrator of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至鄆七日，徙鎮鄜延。

translations.literal: After seven days at Yan, transferred to garrison at Yanyan.
translations.idiomatic: After only seven days at Yan Prefecture he was transferred to command at Yanyan.

sentences.zh: 种諤受嵬名山降，取綏州，夏人遂殺楊定。

translations.literal: Chong E accepted the surrender of Wei Mingshan, took Suizhou; the Xia people then killed Yang Ding.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong E accepted the surrender of Wei Mingshan and seized Suizhou, the Xia killed Yang Ding.

sentences.zh: 朝論以邊釁方起，欲棄綏。

translations.literal: Court opinion held that since border trouble had just begun, they wished to abandon Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion held that with border trouble just beginning, Suizhou should be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 逵曰：「虜既殺王官，而又棄綏不守，見弱已甚。

translations.literal: Kui said: "The barbarians have already killed a royal official, and yet we abandon Suizhou and do not hold it—showing weakness already extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Kui said, "The barbarians have already killed a royal official, and we would abandon Suizhou as well—we would appear utterly weak.

sentences.zh: 且名山舉族來歸，當何以處？

translations.literal: Moreover Mingshan brought his whole clan to submit—how ought he be treated?
translations.idiomatic: And if Mingshan brought his whole clan to submit, how would we treat them?

sentences.zh: 」既而夏人欲以塞門、安遠二砦來易，朝廷許之。

translations.literal: Subsequently the Xia wished to exchange the two stockades Saimen and Anyuan for it; the court consented.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Xia wished to exchange the Saimen and Anyuan stockades for Suizhou, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 逵曰：「此正商於六百里之策也。

translations.literal: Kui said: "This is precisely the policy of the six hundred li of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: Kui said, "This is precisely the policy of ceding six hundred li of Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 非先交二砦，不可與。

translations.literal: Unless the two stockades are first delivered, it cannot be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Unless the two stockades are delivered first, Suizhou must not be given up.

sentences.zh: 」遣其屬趙禼、薛昌朝與夏使議，唯言砦基，禼曰：「二砦之北，舊有三十六堡，且以長城嶺為界，西平王祥符所移書固在也。

translations.literal: He sent his subordinates Zhao Xie and Xue Changchao to discuss with the Xia envoy; they spoke only of stockade foundations; Xie said: "North of the two stockades there were formerly thirty-six forts, and the Changcheng Ridge served as boundary—the letter moved by the Prince of Xiping in the Xiangfu era still exists."
translations.idiomatic: He sent his subordinates Zhao Xie and Xue Changchao to negotiate with the Xia envoy. When the envoy spoke only of stockade foundations, Xie said, "North of the two stockades there had formerly been thirty-six forts, with Changcheng Ridge as the boundary—the letter sent by the Prince of Xiping in the Xiangfu era still survives."

sentences.zh: 」虜使驚不能對，乃寢其請。

translations.literal: The barbarian envoy, startled, could not reply; thereupon their request was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia envoy, startled, could not reply, and the request was dropped.

sentences.zh: 初，詔焚棄綏州，逵匿而不下。

translations.literal: At first an edict ordered burning and abandoning Suizhou; Kui concealed it and did not issue it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier an edict had ordered Suizhou burned and abandoned, but Kui concealed it and never issued the order.

sentences.zh: 至是，帝問大臣，皆莫知，逵始自劾向者違詔旨之罪，帝手詔褒答。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor asked the ministers; none knew; Kui then impeached himself for the crime of earlier violating the edict; the emperor replied with a personal edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked his ministers about it, none knew. Kui then impeached himself for having earlier defied the edict, and the emperor answered with a personal edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 夏人又求以亡命景詢易名山，逵曰：「詢，庸人也，於事何所輕重！

translations.literal: The Xia again sought to exchange the fugitive Jing Xun for Mingshan; Kui said: "Xun is a mediocre man—what weight does he carry in the matter!
translations.idiomatic: The Xia again sought to exchange the fugitive Jing Xun for Mingshan. Kui said, "Xun is a mediocre man—what does he matter in this affair!

sentences.zh: 受之則不得不還名山，恐自是蕃酋無復敢向化矣。

translations.literal: If accepted, one would have no choice but to return Mingshan; I fear from this the barbarian chiefs would no longer dare turn toward civilization.
translations.idiomatic: If we accepted, we would have to return Mingshan, and I fear no tribal chief would dare submit after that.

sentences.zh: 」逵詗得殺楊定者首領姓名，諜告將斬之於境以謝罪，逵曰：「是且梟死囚以紿我。

translations.literal: Kui spied out and learned the names of the leaders who killed Yang Ding; a spy reported they would behead them at the border to apologize; Kui said: "They will merely display executed convicts to deceive us.
translations.idiomatic: Kui learned through espionage the names of the leaders who had killed Yang Ding. When a spy reported the Xia would behead them at the border as an apology, Kui said, "They will merely parade executed convicts to deceive us.

sentences.zh: 」報曰：「必執李崇貴、韓道喜來。

translations.literal: He replied: "You must bring Li Chonggui and Han Daoxi here."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "You must deliver Li Chonggui and Han Daoxi."

sentences.zh: 」夏人言：「殺之矣。

translations.literal: The Xia said: "We have killed them."
translations.idiomatic: The Xia said, "We have killed them.

sentences.zh: 」逵命以二人狀貌物色詰問虜，情得，乃執獻之。

translations.literal: Kui ordered that the two men's appearances be used to identify and question the barbarians; the facts were established; thereupon they were seized and presented.
translations.idiomatic: Kui had the two men's appearances used to identify and question the Xia envoys; when the truth came out, the men were seized and delivered.

sentences.zh: 加檢校太尉、雄武軍留後。

translations.literal: Added as Honorary Grand Commandant and Military Commissioner of the Xiongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed honorary grand commandant and military commissioner of the Xiongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 韓絳主种諤計圖橫山，與逵議出兵。

translations.literal: Han Jiang championed Chong E's plan to seize Hengshan and discussed dispatching troops with Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jiang backed Chong E's plan to seize Hengshan and discussed sending troops with Kui.

sentences.zh: 逵曰：「諤，狂生爾，朝廷徒以家世用之，必誤大事。

translations.literal: Kui said: "E is a wild young man; the court employs him only because of his family—he will surely ruin a great affair."
translations.idiomatic: Kui said, "E is a reckless young man whom the court employs only for his family name—he will surely ruin everything.

sentences.zh: 」絳怒，以為沮撓，奏召逵還。

translations.literal: Jiang was angry, regarded it as obstruction, and memorialized to recall Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang was furious, took this as obstruction, and memorialized to recall Kui.

sentences.zh: 明年，慶州亂，出判永興，徙秦州。

translations.literal: The next year Qingzhou rebelled; sent out to administer Yongxing, transferred to Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Qingzhou rebelled, he was sent out to administer Yongxing and then transferred to Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 王韶開熙河，逵案其不法。

translations.literal: Wang Shao opened Xihe; Kui investigated his illegal conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shao opened Xihe, Kui investigated his illegal conduct.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣蔡確鞫之，謂逵誣罔，落宣徽使、知潞州。

translations.literal: The court sent Cai Que to try the case; held that Kui had framed falsely; stripped of Privy Pavilion commissioner, made Prefect of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Cai Que to try the case, found that Kui had made false accusations, stripped him of his privy pavilion commission, and made him prefect of Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 徙太原，復宣徽使。

translations.literal: Transferred to Taiyuan; restored as Privy Pavilion commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Taiyuan and restored as privy pavilion commissioner.

sentences.zh: 交阯李乾德陷邕管，召為安南行營經略招討使兼荊湖、廣南宣撫使，請鄜延、河東舊吏士自隨。

translations.literal: Jiaozhi's Li Qiande captured Yong and Guan; recalled as Pacification and Suppression Commissioner of the Annam Field Headquarters and concurrently Pacification Commissioner of Jinghu and Guangnan; requested old clerks and officers from Yanyan and Hedong to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Qiande of Jiaozhi captured Yong and Guan, Kui was recalled as pacification and suppression commissioner of the Annam field headquarters and concurrently pacification commissioner of Jinghu and Guangnan. He asked to bring old clerks and officers from Yanyan and Hedong with him.

sentences.zh: 將行，宴於便殿，賜中軍旗章劍甲以示寵。

translations.literal: About to depart, feasted in the Privy Hall; granted central army flags, insignia, sword, and armor to show favor.
translations.idiomatic: Before departing he was feasted in the Privy Hall and granted the central army flags, insignia, sword, and armor as a mark of imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 次長沙，先遣將復邕、廉；

translations.literal: Stopping at Changsha, first sent generals to recover Yong and Lian;
translations.idiomatic: At Changsha he first sent generals to recover Yong and Lian;

sentences.zh: 至廣西，討拔廣源州，降守將劉應紀；

translations.literal: Reaching Guangxi, attacked and captured Guangyuan Prefecture, accepting the surrender of defending general Liu Yingji;
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Guangxi, he captured Guangyuan Prefecture and accepted the surrender of its defending general Liu Yingji;

sentences.zh: 又拔決裏隘，乘勝取桄榔、門州，大戰富良江，斬偽王子洪真。

translations.literal: Also captured Jueli Pass, pressed the victory to take Guanglang and Men Prefectures, fought a great battle at the Fu River, beheaded the false prince Hong Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He also took Jueli Pass, pressed the advantage to seize Guanglang and Men Prefectures, fought a great battle on the Fu River, and beheaded the pretender's prince Hong Zhen.

sentences.zh: 乾德窮蹙，奉表歸命。

translations.literal: Qiande, pressed to extremity, submitted a memorial surrendering to the command.
