translations.idiomatic: Qiande, driven to extremity, submitted a memorial surrendering to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 時兵夫三十萬人，冒暑涉瘴地，死者過半。

translations.literal: At the time soldiers and laborers numbered three hundred thousand; braving heat they crossed malarial lands; more than half died.
translations.idiomatic: At the time three hundred thousand soldiers and laborers braved heat and crossed malarial lands; more than half died.

sentences.zh: 至是，與賊隔一水不得進，乃班師。

translations.literal: At this point, separated from the bandits by one river and unable to advance, thereupon withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: At that point, separated from the enemy by a river and unable to advance, he withdrew the army.

sentences.zh: 坐貶左衛將軍，西京安置，屏處十年。

translations.literal: On that account demoted to General of the Left Guard, settled in the Western Capital, kept in seclusion for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: On that account he was demoted to general of the Left Guard, settled in the Western Capital, and kept in seclusion for ten years.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，復左屯衛大將軍致仕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong acceded, restored as Great General of the Left Tunwei Guard and granted retirement.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong acceded, he was restored as great general of the Left Tunwei Guard and granted retirement.

sentences.zh: 起知潞州，進廣州觀察使、知河中。

translations.literal: Recalled to serve as Prefect of Lu; advanced to Observer of Guangzhou and Prefect of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Lu Prefecture, then promoted to observer of Guangzhou and prefect of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 辭歸洛，改左武衛上將軍、提舉崇福宮，卒。

translations.literal: Declined and returned to Luoyang; changed to Senior General of the Left Wuwei Guard and Director of the Chongfu Palace; died.
translations.idiomatic: He declined office and returned to Luoyang, was made senior general of the Left Wuwei Guard and director of the Chongfu Palace, and died.

sentences.zh: 輟視朝一日，贈雄武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Court audience was suspended for one day; posthumously granted Military Commissioner of the Xiongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Court audience was suspended for one day, and he was posthumously granted the title of military commissioner of the Xiongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 逵忼慨喜兵學，神宗嘗訪八陣遺法，對曰：「兵無常形，是特奇正相生之一法爾。

translations.literal: Kui was forthright and ardent, fond of military studies; Emperor Shenzong once inquired about the remnant methods of the Eight Formations; he replied: "War has no fixed form—this is merely one method among those by which direct and indirect forces give rise to each other."
translations.idiomatic: Kui was forthright and passionate, and loved the study of war. When Emperor Shenzong once asked about the surviving methods of the Eight Formations, he replied, "War has no fixed form—this is merely one method by which direct and indirect forces give rise to each other.

sentences.zh: 」因為帝論其詳。

translations.literal: Thereupon he expounded the details for the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He then expounded the details for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 在延安，使以教兵，久不就。

translations.literal: At Yan'an, he was ordered to drill troops, but for a long time he did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: At Yan'an he was ordered to drill the troops, but for a long time made no progress.

sentences.zh: 逵擇諸校習金鼓屯營者六十四人，使人教一隊，頃刻而成。

translations.literal: Kui selected sixty-four officers skilled in gongs, drums, encampment, and garrison; had each man train one squad; in an instant it was accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Kui selected sixty-four officers skilled in gongs, drums, encampment, and garrison, had each train one squad, and in no time the drill was complete.

sentences.zh: 尤善用偏裨，每至所部，令人自言所能，暇日閱按之，故臨陣皆盡其技。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in using junior officers; whenever he reached his command, he had men state their own abilities; on free days he reviewed and tested them; therefore in battle all gave their full skill.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled at using junior officers. Whenever he arrived at his command he had men declare their own abilities and tested them on free days, so in battle each gave his full skill.

sentences.zh: 李復圭治慶州之敗，既斬李信、劉甫，又欲罪鄜延都巡檢使白玉。

translations.literal: Li Fugui dealt with the defeat at Qingzhou; having already executed Li Xin and Liu Fu, he also wished to punish Yanyan Circuit Inspector Bai Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Fugui investigated the defeat at Qingzhou, having already executed Li Xin and Liu Fu, he also sought to punish Yanyan circuit inspector Bai Yu.

sentences.zh: 玉見逵託以後事，且泣言不得終養母。

translations.literal: Yu visited Kui and entrusted him with affairs after death, weeping as he said he could not finish caring for his mother in her old age.
translations.idiomatic: Yu visited Kui and entrusted him with his affairs after death, weeping that he would not be able to care for his mother through her final years.

sentences.zh: 逵哀之，不遣，申救甚力，得免。

translations.literal: Kui pitied him, did not send him away, pleaded his case with great force, and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Kui pitied him, refused to let him go, and pleaded his case with great force until he was spared.

sentences.zh: 已而玉大捷於新砦，神宗謂逵曰：「白玉能以功補過，卿之力也。

translations.literal: Before long Yu won a great victory at Xincheng; Emperor Shenzong said to Kui: "Bai Yu was able to make up for faults with merit—this is your doing."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yu won a great victory at Xincheng. Emperor Shenzong said to Kui, "Bai Yu was able to redeem his faults with merit—this is your doing.

sentences.zh: 」每戰，先招懷，後戰鬥，愛惜士卒，不妄加誅戮。

translations.literal: In every battle he first sought to win over and pacify, then fought; he cherished his soldiers and did not recklessly impose punishments of death.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle he first tried to win over the enemy and only then fought. He cherished his soldiers and did not impose death punishments recklessly.

sentences.zh: 其殺賊婦女老弱者，皆不賞。

translations.literal: Those who killed bandit women, the old, and the weak were all unrewarded.
translations.idiomatic: He gave no rewards to those who killed enemy women, the old, or the weak.

sentences.zh: 雖坐征南無功久廢，猶隱然為一時宿將云。

translations.literal: Though on account of the southern campaign's failure he was long set aside, he still remained implicitly a veteran general of the age, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Though the failed southern campaign had long sidelined him, he remained, it was said, a veteran general of his age.

sentences.zh: 論曰：宋至仁宗時，承平百年，武夫鷙卒遭時致位者雖有之，起健卒至政府，隱然為時名將，惟青與逵兩人爾。

translations.literal: The discussion says: When Song reached Emperor Renzong's time, after a century of peace, fierce warriors and stern soldiers who met the moment and rose to position did exist; but to rise from stalwart soldier to the government and implicitly become a renowned general of the age—only Qing and Kui, two men.
translations.idiomatic: The discussion runs thus: By Emperor Renzong's reign the Song had enjoyed a century of peace. Fierce warriors and tough soldiers who rose with the times were not unknown, but to rise from common soldier to the halls of government and stand as a celebrated general of the age—only Di Qing and Guo Kui.

sentences.zh: 青在邊境凡二十五戰，無大勝，亦無大敗，最後崑崙一舉，頗著奇雋。

translations.literal: Qing on the border fought twenty-five battles in all; no great victory, nor any great defeat; the final Kunlun action was markedly distinguished for its singular brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Qing fought twenty-five battles on the frontier—no great victory, yet no great defeat either. His final action at Kunlun was notably brilliant.

sentences.zh: 考其識量，亦過人遠矣。

translations.literal: Examining his discernment and capacity, he also surpassed others by far.
translations.idiomatic: When one considers his discernment and capacity, he too far surpassed ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 逵料葛懷敏之敗，如燭照龜卜，一時最為知兵。

translations.literal: Kui foresaw Ge Huaimin's defeat as clearly as candlelight illuminates or tortoise-shell divination reveals—the most knowledgeable in war of his time.
translations.idiomatic: Kui foresaw Ge Huaimin's defeat as clearly as candlelight or tortoise-shell divination—the foremost military mind of his age.

sentences.zh: 雖南征無功，用違其長，又何尤焉。

translations.literal: Though the southern expedition achieved no merit, his talent was used against its strength—what blame is there?
translations.idiomatic: Though the southern expedition came to nothing, his talent was put to the wrong use—how can he be blamed for that?
